sentences.zh: 【齊紀十】　重光大荒落，一年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 10] Chongshen, Great Barren Fall, one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 10] The first year of the Chongshen era (Great Barren Fall).

sentences.zh: 和皇帝中興元年（

translations.literal: First year of Zhongxing of Emperor He (
translations.idiomatic: First year of the Zhongxing ("Restoration") era of Emperor He (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元五零一年）

translations.literal: xinsi, the year 501 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinsi [cyclical date], equivalent to 501 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉，東昏侯以晉安王寶義為司徒，建安王寶寅為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, dingyou, the Marquis of Eastern Depravity made Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi Grand Tutor and Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin General of Chariots and Cavalry with office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingyou, Marquis Donghun appointed Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi Grand Tutor and Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege to maintain an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，南康王寶融始稱相國，大赦；

translations.literal: Yisi, Prince of Nankang Bao Rong first took the title Chancellor of State and proclaimed a general amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Prince of Nankang Bao Rong first assumed the title of Chancellor of State and proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 以蕭穎冑為左長史，蕭衍為征東將軍，楊公則為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiao Yingzhou Left Chief Secretary, Xiao Yan General Who Conquers the East, and Yang Gongze Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiao Yingmou Senior Secretary of the Left, Xiao Yan General Who Conquers the East, and Yang Gongze Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 戊申，蕭衍發襄陽，留弟偉總府州事，憺守壘城，府司馬莊丘黑守樊城。

translations.literal: Wushen, Xiao Yan set out from Xiangyang, leaving his younger brother Wei in overall charge of prefectural affairs, Dan to guard Lei City, and Prefectural Major Zhuangqiu Hei to guard Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Xiao Yan marched from Xiangyang, leaving his younger brother Wei to oversee prefectural and district affairs, Dan to hold Lei City, and the prefectural major Zhuangqiu Hei to defend Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 衍既行，州中兵及儲偫皆虛。

translations.literal: Once Yan had departed, the province's troops and stored provisions were all depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan had left, the province's troops and reserve stores were entirely exhausted.

sentences.zh: 魏興太守裴師仁、齊興太守顏僧都並不受衍命，舉兵欲襲襄陽，偉、憺遣兵邀擊於治平，大破之，雍州乃安。

translations.literal: Pei Shiren, Administrator of Weixing, and Yan Sengdu, Administrator of Qixing, both refused to obey Yan's orders and raised troops intending to strike Xiangyang; Wei and Dan sent troops to intercept them at Zhiping, inflicted a great defeat, and Yong Province was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shiren, prefect of Weixing, and Yan Sengdu, prefect of Qixing, both defied Yan's orders and raised armies to attack Xiangyang. Wei and Dan dispatched forces to intercept them at Zhiping, routed them utterly, and Yong Province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 魏咸陽王禧為上相，不親政務，驕奢貪淫，多為不法，魏主頗惡之。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xi, served as chief minister but did not personally attend to government affairs; arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and licentious, he committed many unlawful acts, and the Wei emperor came to dislike him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xi of Xianyang served as chief minister of Northern Wei but took no part in state affairs himself. Arrogant, lavish, greedy, and dissolute, he broke the law repeatedly, and the Wei emperor grew deeply displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 禧遣奴就領軍於烈求舊羽林虎賁，執仗出入。

translations.literal: Xi sent a slave to the Commandant of Guards Yu Lie to request the former Tiger Guards of the Feathered Forest to carry weapons and escort him in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent a servant to Yu Lie, Commandant of Guards, to demand the veteran Tiger Guards of the Feathered Forest to bear arms and attend him whenever he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 烈曰：「天子諒暗，事歸宰輔。

translations.literal: Lie said: "The Son of Heaven is in mourning seclusion; affairs belong to the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Lie replied, "The Son of Heaven remains in mourning seclusion; all affairs rest with the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 領軍但知典掌宿衛，非有詔不敢違理從私。

translations.literal: "The Commandant of Guards knows only how to oversee palace guards. Without an imperial edict I dare not violate regulation to grant a private favor."
translations.idiomatic: "As Commandant of Guards, I am charged only with palace security. Without an imperial edict I will not bend the rules for a private request."

sentences.zh: 」禧奴惘然而返。

translations.literal: Xi's slave returned in a daze.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's servant went away baffled and empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 禧復遣謂烈曰：「我，天子之子，天子叔父，身為元輔，有所求須，與詔何異！

translations.literal: Xi again sent someone to tell Lie: "I am the Son of Heaven's son, the Son of Heaven's uncle, and I serve as chief minister—a request from me differs little from an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent word again: "I am the emperor's son and his uncle, and I hold the chief ministership. What difference does my demand make from an edict?"

sentences.zh: 」烈厲色曰：「烈非不知王之貴也，奈何使私奴索天子羽林！

translations.literal: Lie said sternly: "Lie is not ignorant of Your Highness's station—how can you send a private slave to demand the Son of Heaven's Feathered Forest guards!"
translations.idiomatic: Lie said sharply, "Lie knows perfectly well how exalted you are—yet how dare you use a private servant to demand the emperor's Feathered Forest guards!"

sentences.zh: 烈頭可得，羽林不可得！

translations.literal: "Lie may give you his head, but you will not have the Feathered Forest guards!"
translations.idiomatic: "You may have Lie's head—but you will not have the Feathered Forest guards!"

sentences.zh: 」禧怒，以烈為恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Xi grew angry and appointed Lie Governor of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, furious, made Lie Governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 烈不願出外，固辭，不許；

translations.literal: Lie did not wish to leave the capital and firmly declined; his refusal was not accepted;
translations.idiomatic: Lie wished to remain at court and pleaded repeatedly to stay; the emperor would not allow it;

sentences.zh: 遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: he therefore claimed illness and would not go out.
translations.idiomatic: he then pleaded sickness and refused to leave his home.

sentences.zh: 烈子左中郎將忠領直閣，常在魏主左右。

translations.literal: Lie's son Zhong, a Left Palace Gentleman-General, commanded the Direct Access Guard and was constantly at the Wei emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's son Zhong, a Left Palace Gentleman-General in charge of the Direct Access Guard, was always close to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 烈使忠言於魏主曰：「諸王專恣，意不可測。

translations.literal: Lie had Zhong speak to the Wei emperor, saying: "The princes act willfully—their intentions cannot be predicted."
translations.idiomatic: Lie had Zhong tell the emperor, "The princes wield unchecked power; their intentions cannot be foreseen."

sentences.zh: 宜早罷之，自攬權綱。

translations.literal: "You should remove them early and take the reins of authority yourself."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty should dismiss them soon and take the reins of government into your own hands."

sentences.zh: 」北海王詳亦密以禧過惡白帝，且言彭城王勰大得人情，不宜久輔政。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai, Yuan Xiang, also secretly reported Xi's faults and crimes to the emperor, and said that Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie had won great popularity and should not assist government for long.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xiang of Beihai also privately reported Xi's misdeeds to the emperor, adding that Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie had won extraordinary favor among the people and ought not remain in power indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 時將礿祭，王公並齋於廟東坊。

translations.literal: When the time came for the yue sacrifice, the kings and dukes all fasted in the east wing of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: As the yue sacrifice approached, princes and grandees all kept ritual abstinence in the temple's eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 帝夜使於忠語烈：「明旦入見，當有處分。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone by night through Zhong to tell Lie: "Enter audience tomorrow morning; there will be orders for you."
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor sent Zhong to tell Lie, "Come to audience tomorrow at dawn; your assignment will be decided then."

sentences.zh: 」質明，烈至。

translations.literal: At daybreak Lie arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At first light Lie came.

sentences.zh: 帝命烈將直閣等六十餘人，宣旨召禧、勰、詳，衛送至帝所。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lie to lead more than sixty men of the Direct Access Guard to proclaim the decree summoning Xi, Xie, and Xiang, and escort them to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lie, with more than sixty Direct Access guards, to summon Xi, Xie, and Xiang by imperial decree and escort them to the throne room.

sentences.zh: 禧等入見於光極殿，帝曰：「恪雖寡昧，忝承寶歷。

translations.literal: Xi and the others entered audience at the Hall of Radiant Pole; the emperor said: "Ke, though dull and benighted, has the honor to inherit the sacred succession."
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others were brought before the Hall of Radiant Pole. The emperor said, "Though I, Ke, am dull and unworthy, I have inherited the throne."

sentences.zh: 比纏尪疹，實憑諸父，苟延視息，奄涉三齡。

translations.literal: "Lately racked by lingering illness, I truly relied on my royal uncles to prolong my breath; this has already spanned three years."
translations.idiomatic: "Lately, consumed by lingering illness, I have truly depended on my uncles merely to draw breath—and that has already stretched to three years."

sentences.zh: 諸父歸遜殷勤，今便親攝百揆。

translations.literal: "My uncles have labored with devoted humility; today I shall personally oversee the hundred offices."
translations.idiomatic: "You have served with unstinting humility; from today I shall personally direct the affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 且還府司，當別處分。

translations.literal: "Return now to your residences; separate orders will follow."
translations.idiomatic: "Return to your mansions for now; further disposition will be made in due course."

sentences.zh: 」又謂勰曰：「頃來南北務殷，不容仰遂沖操。

translations.literal: To Xie he said: "Recently north and south affairs have been pressing; I could not allow you to retire according to your lofty resolve."
translations.idiomatic: To Xie he said, "North and south affairs have pressed hard of late; I could not let you withdraw to honor your wish for seclusion."

sentences.zh: 恪是何人，而敢久違先敕，今遂叔父高蹈之意。

translations.literal: "What sort of man is Ke, that he would dare long defy the late emperor's charge? Today I grant my uncle's wish for the high and reclusive life."
translations.idiomatic: "Who am I, Ke, to keep you from the late emperor's command any longer? Today I grant you the seclusion you have long desired."

sentences.zh: 」勰謝曰：「陛下孝恭，仰遵先詔，上成睿明之美，下遂微臣之志，感今惟往，悲喜交深。

translations.literal: Xie thanked him: "Your Majesty is filial and respectful, reverently following the late emperor's charge—achieving enlightened brilliance above and granting this humble servant's wish below. I feel the present by the past; joy and grief mingle deep within."
translations.idiomatic: Xie bowed and said, "Your Majesty's filial reverence in honoring the late emperor's charge perfects enlightened rule above and fulfills this humble servant's wish below. Memory of the past floods the present; joy and sorrow are intertwined beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，詔勰以王歸第；

translations.literal: On gengxu an edict sent Prince Xie home to his mansion;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor ordered Xie to return to his princely residence;

sentences.zh: 禧進位太保；

translations.literal: Xi was promoted to Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Xi was advanced to Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 詳為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Xiang was made Grand General and Supervisor of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was appointed Grand General with charge over the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尚書清河張彝、邢巒聞處分非常，亡走，出洛陽城，為御史中尉中山甄琛所彈。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi of Qinghe and Xing Luan, Masters of Writing, hearing of the extraordinary disposition, fled outside Luoyang and were impeached by the Censor-in-Chief Zhen Chen of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi of Qinghe and Xing Luan, both Masters of Writing, hearing of these extraordinary moves, fled the city. The Censor-in-Chief Zhen Chen of Zhongshan impeached them for deserting Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔書切責之。

translations.literal: An imperial edict sternly reproved them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply censured them.

sentences.zh: 復以於烈為領軍，仍加車騎大將軍，自是長直禁中，軍國大事，皆得參焉。

translations.literal: Yu Lie was again made Commandant of Guards and additionally Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; from then on he kept constant duty within the palace, and all great military and civil affairs were subject to his participation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lie was restored as Commandant of Guards and additionally made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry. Henceforth he kept permanent watch within the palace precincts, and on all major military and civil matters he had a voice.

sentences.zh: 魏主時年十六，不能親決庶務，委之左右。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was then sixteen and could not personally decide ordinary affairs, delegating them to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was only sixteen. Unable to decide routine business himself, he left it to his intimates.

sentences.zh: 於是幸臣茹皓、趙郡王仲興、上谷寇猛、趙郡趙修、南陽趙邕及外戚高肇等始用事，魏政浸衰。

translations.literal: Thereupon favorites Ru Hao, Wang Zhongxing of Zhaojun, Kou Meng of Shanggu, Zhao Xiu of Zhaojun, Zhao Yong of Nanyang, and the empress's kin Gao Zhao and others began to wield power, and Wei governance gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites Ru Hao, Wang Zhongxing of Zhaojun, Kou Meng of Shanggu, Zhao Xiu and Zhao Yong of their respective commanderies, together with the empress's kin Gao Zhao, now took charge, and Wei administration steadily deteriorated.

sentences.zh: 趙修尤親幸，旬月間，累遷至光祿卿；

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu was especially favored; within ten days and a month he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu enjoyed the deepest favor and within mere weeks was promoted repeatedly until he reached Director of the Imperial Clan;

sentences.zh: 每遷官，帝親至其宅設宴，王公百官皆從。

translations.literal: each time he was promoted the emperor personally came to his house to host a feast, and kings, dukes, and all officials followed.
translations.idiomatic: at every promotion the emperor went in person to his home to give a banquet, and princes, grandees, and the entire bureaucracy attended.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，東昏侯祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinhai Marquis Donghun sacrificed at the Southern Suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Marquis Donghun performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏主引見群臣於太極前殿，告以親政之意。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Wei emperor summoned the officials to audience in the front hall of Taiji and announced his intention to take personal governance.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Wei emperor received the full court in the front hall of Taiji and declared his intention to rule in person.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以咸陽王禧領太尉，廣陵王羽為司。

translations.literal: On renxu Prince Xi of Xianyang was made concurrent Grand Commandant, and Prince Yu of Guangling Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Prince Xi of Xianyang was appointed concurrent Grand Commandant, and Prince Yu of Guangling Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 魏主引羽入內，面授之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor brought Yu inside and invested him in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led Yu within the palace and invested him with the seal in person.

sentences.zh: 羽固辭曰：「彥和本自不願，而陛下強與之。

translations.literal: Yu firmly declined, saying: "Yanhe never wished it, yet Your Majesty forcibly gave it to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yu pleaded firmly, "Yanhe never wanted the post, yet Your Majesty compelled him to accept it."

sentences.zh: 今新去此官而以臣代之，必招物議。

translations.literal: "Now he has just left this office and Your Majesty would replace him with me—this is sure to draw public criticism."
translations.idiomatic: "He has only just been relieved, and to give the office to me at once will certainly draw criticism."

sentences.zh: 」乃以為司空。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was therefore appointed Minister of Works instead.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，南康王以冠軍長史王茂為江州刺史，竟陵太守曹景宗為郢州刺史，邵陵王寶修為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, yichou, Prince of Nankang made Champion Chief Secretary Wang Mao Governor of Jiangzhou, Jingling Administrator Cao Jingzong Governor of Yingzhou, and Prince of Shaoling Bao Xiu Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, Prince of Nankang appointed Wang Mao, chief secretary of the Champion's staff, Governor of Jiang Province, Cao Jingzong, prefect of Jingling, Governor of Ying Province, and Prince of Shaoling Bao Xiu Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the Northern Wei court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 壬午，東昏侯遣羽林兵擊雍州，中外纂嚴。

translations.literal: On renwu Marquis Donghun sent Feathered Forest troops to attack Yongzhou, and within and without the realm tightened defense.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Marquis Donghun dispatched Feathered Forest troops against Yong Province; throughout the realm defenses were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 甲申，蕭衍至竟陵，命王茂、曹景宗為前軍，以中兵參國張法安守竟陵城。

translations.literal: On jiashen Xiao Yan reached Jingling, made Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong the vanguard, and left Central Army Major Zhang Fa'an to guard Jingling city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Xiao Yan reached Jingling, appointed Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong to lead the vanguard, and left Central Army Major Zhang Fa'an to hold Jingling city.

sentences.zh: 茂等至漢口，諸將議欲並兵圍郢，分兵襲西陽、武昌。

translations.literal: When Mao and the others reached Hankou, the generals debated concentrating forces to besiege Ying and sending detachments to strike Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao and the others reached Hankou, the generals debated massing their armies to besiege Ying while sending detachments against Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「漢口不闊一里，箭道交至，房僧寄以重兵固守，與郢城為掎角；

translations.literal: Yan said: "Hankou is less than a li across; arrows fly from every direction. Fang Sengji holds it with a heavy force in mutual support with Ying city;
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Hankou is scarcely a li wide, and arrows can strike from every side. Fang Sengji holds it with a large force in concert with Ying city;

sentences.zh: 若悉眾前進，僧寄必絕我軍後，悔無所及。

translations.literal: if we advance with our entire force, Sengji is sure to cut off our rear—regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: if we advance with our entire army, Sengji will surely cut off our rear, and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 不若遣王、曹諸軍濟江，與荊州軍合，以逼郢城；

translations.literal: "Better to send Wang, Cao, and the other armies across the river to join the Jingzhou forces and press Ying city;
translations.idiomatic: "Better to send Wang, Cao, and the other armies across the river to join the Jingzhou troops and press Ying city;

sentences.zh: 吾自圍魯山以通沔、漢，使鄖城、竟陵之粟方舟而下，江陵、湘中之兵相繼而至，兵多食足，何憂兩城之不拔！

translations.literal: I myself will besiege Lushan to open the Mian and Han routes, have grain from Yuncheng and Jingling float down in linked boats, and troops from Jiangling and Xiangzhong arrive in succession—when soldiers are many and food ample, why worry that the two cities will not fall!"
translations.idiomatic: I will myself besiege Lushan to open the Mian and Han waterways, float grain from Yuncheng and Jingling downriver in convoys, and bring troops from Jiangling and the Xiang region in succession. With ample men and provisions, why should either city hold out?"

sentences.zh: 天下之事，可以臥取之耳。

translations.literal: "The affairs of the realm can be taken while lying down."
translations.idiomatic: "The empire can be won from one's couch."

sentences.zh: 」乃使茂等帥眾濟江，頓九里。

translations.literal: He then had Mao and the others lead the army across the river and encamp at Jiuli.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Mao and the others lead their forces across the river and encamp at Jiuli.

sentences.zh: 張沖遣中兵參軍陳光靜開門迎戰，茂等擊破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong sent Central Army Major Chen Guangjing to open the gates and give battle; Mao and the others defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong sent Central Army Major Chen Guangjing out to give battle; Mao and the others routed him.

sentences.zh: 光靜死，沖嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Guangjing died, and Chong tied himself to the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjing was killed, and Chong shut himself within the city to hold out.

sentences.zh: 景宗遂據石橋浦，連軍相續，下至加湖。

translations.literal: Jingzong then seized Shiqiao Ford, linking camps in succession down to Jiahu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong then seized Shiqiao Ford and strung his camps in succession down to Jiahu.

sentences.zh: 荊州遣冠軍將軍鄧元起、軍主王世興、田安之將數千人會雍州兵於夏首。

translations.literal: Jingzhou sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi and army commanders Wang Shixing and Tian Anzhi with several thousand men to join Yongzhou troops at Xiashou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi and army commanders Wang Shixing and Tian Anzhi with several thousand men to join Yong Province forces at Xiashou.

sentences.zh: 衍築漢口城以守魯山，命水軍主義陽張惠紹等游遏江中，絕郢、魯二城信使。

translations.literal: Yan built Hankou city to hold Lushan, and ordered naval commander Zhang Huishao of Yiyang and others to patrol the river and cut off messengers between Ying and Lu cities.
translations.idiomatic: Yan built Hankou city to hold Lushan and ordered naval commander Zhang Huishao of Yiyang and others to patrol the river, severing communications between Ying and Lu.

sentences.zh: 楊公則舉湘州之眾會於夏口。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze raised the masses of Xiangzhou and assembled at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze mustered the forces of Xiang Province and joined the assembly at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎冑命荊州諸軍皆受公則節度，雖蕭穎達亦隸焉。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingzhou ordered all Jingzhou armies to accept Gongze's command, and even Xiao Yingda was placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingmou ordered all Jing Province armies to accept Yang Gongze's command, and even Xiao Yingda was placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 府朝儀欲遣人行湘州事而難其人，西中郎中兵參軍劉坦謂眾曰：「湘土人情，易擾難信，用武士則浸漁百姓，用文士則威略不振；

translations.literal: The prefectural court wished to send someone to administer Xiangzhou affairs but found no suitable man. Western Palace Gentleman and Central Army Major Liu Tan said to the assembly: "The customs of Xiang people are easily stirred and hard to trust; employ a warrior and he will prey on the people, employ a scholar and authority will not hold;"
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural court wished to send someone to administer Xiang Province but could find no suitable candidate. Western Palace Gentleman and Central Army Major Liu Tan told the assembly, "The people of Xiang are quick to stir and slow to trust. Appoint a warrior and he will prey on the populace; appoint a scholar and authority will not hold."

sentences.zh: 必欲鎮靜一州，軍民足食，無逾老夫。

translations.literal: "if you must pacify a province and keep soldiers and people fed, none surpasses this old man."
translations.idiomatic: "If you must pacify the province and keep soldiers and civilians fed, there is no one better than this old man."

sentences.zh: 」乃以坦為輔國長史、長沙太守，行湘州事。

translations.literal: Tan was therefore made Chief Secretary Assisting the State and Administrator of Changsha, acting for Xiangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was therefore appointed Chief Secretary Assisting the State and Prefect of Changsha, with charge of Xiang Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 坦先嘗在湘州，多舊恩，迎者屬路。

translations.literal: Tan had previously served in Xiangzhou and had many old obligations of favor; those who came to welcome him lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had served in Xiang Province before and had won many old obligations of gratitude; welcomers lined the road.

sentences.zh: 下車，選堪事吏分詣十郡，發民運租米三十餘萬斛以助荊、雍之軍，由是資糧不乏。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he selected capable clerks to go to the ten commanderies, mobilized the people to transport more than three hundred thousand hu of tax rice to aid the Jing and Yong armies, and thereby supplies did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office he selected capable clerks and sent them to the ten commanderies, mobilized the people to transport more than three hundred thousand hu of tax grain to support the Jing and Yong armies, and thereby supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 三月，蕭衍使鄧元起進據南堂西渚，田安之頓城北，王世興頓曲水故城。

translations.literal: Third month, Xiao Yan had Deng Yuanqi advance and seize the western islet of the Southern Hall; Tian Anzhi encamped north of the city, Wang Shixing encamped at the old city of Qu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Xiao Yan had Deng Yuanqi advance and seize the western islet of the Southern Hall; Tian Anzhi encamped north of the city and Wang Shixing at the old city of Qu River.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，張沖病卒，驍騎將軍薛元嗣與沖子孜及征虜長史江夏內史程茂共守郢城。

translations.literal: On dingyou Zhang Chong died of illness; Valiant Cavalry General Xue Yuansi, Chong's son Zi, and Campaign General Chief Secretary and Jiangxia Interior Minister Cheng Mao jointly defended Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Zhang Chong died of illness. Valiant Cavalry General Xue Yuansi, Chong's son Zi, and Campaign General Chief Secretary and Jiangxia interior minister Cheng Mao jointly held Ying city.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，南康王即皇帝位於江陵，改元，大赦，立宗廟、南北郊，州府城門悉依建康宮，置尚書五省，以南郡太守為尹，以蕭穎冑為尚書令，蕭衍為左僕射，晉安王寶義為司空，廬陵王寶源為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，建安王寶寅為徐州刺史，散騎常侍夏侯詳為中領軍，冠軍將軍蕭偉為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On yisi Prince of Nankang assumed the imperial throne at Jiangling, changed the era name, proclaimed a general amnesty, established the ancestral temple and suburban altars, made all prefectural and district gates follow the Jiankang palace pattern, established the five departments of the Masters of Writing, made the Administrator of Nan commandery metropolitan magistrate, made Xiao Yingzhou Director of the Masters of Writing, Xiao Yan Left Vice Director, Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi Minister of Works, Prince of Luling Bao Yuan General of Chariots and Cavalry with office equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin Governor of Xuzhou, Palace Attendant Xiahou Xiang Commandant of the Center Army, and Champion General Xiao Wei Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Prince of Nankang took the throne at Jiangling, changed the era name, and proclaimed a general amnesty. He established the ancestral temple and the suburban altars, modeled prefectural and district gates on the Jiankang palace, and set up the five departments of the Masters of Writing. The prefect of Nan commandery became metropolitan magistrate; Xiao Yingmou was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Xiao Yan, Left Vice Director; Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi, Minister of Works; Prince of Luling Bao Yuan, General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies; Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, Governor of Xu Province; Palace Attendant Xiahou Xiang, Commandant of the Center Army; and Champion General Xiao Wei, Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔封庶人寶卷為涪陵王。

translations.literal: On bingwu an edict enfeoffed the commoner Bao Juan as Prince of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu an edict enfeoffed the deposed emperor Bao Juan as Prince of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以尚書令蕭穎冑行荊州刺史，加蕭衍征東大將軍、都督征討諸軍事，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: On yiyou Xiao Yingzhou as Director of the Masters of Writing was made acting Governor of Jingzhou; Xiao Yan was added as General Who Conquers the East and Director of All Campaign and Punitive Forces, with the yellow battle-axe conferred.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Xiao Yingmou, as Director of the Masters of Writing, was made acting Governor of Jing Province; Xiao Yan was promoted to General Who Conquers the East and made supreme commander of all campaign forces, with the yellow battle-axe conferred.

sentences.zh: 時衍次楊口，和帝遣御史中丞宗夬勞軍。

translations.literal: At the time Yan was stationed at Yangkou; Emperor He sent Imperial Censor Zong Que to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was then stationed at Yangkou; Emperor He sent Imperial Censor Zong Que to comfort the army.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍新野庾域諷夬曰：「黃鉞未加，非所以總帥侯伯。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the North General Yu Yu of Xinye hinted to Que: "Without the yellow battle-axe conferred, this is not how one commands the feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier of the North General Yu Yu of Xinye hinted to Que, "Without the yellow battle-axe, how can he command the feudal lords?"

sentences.zh: 」夬返西台，遂有是命。

translations.literal: Que returned to the western capital and thereupon came this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Que returned to the western capital, and the appointment followed.

sentences.zh: 薜元嗣遣軍主沈難當帥輕舸數千亂流來戰，張惠紹等擊擒之。

translations.literal: Xue Yuansi sent army commander Shen Nandang with several thousand light boats to fight upstream in disorder; Zhang Huishao and others attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuansi sent army commander Shen Nandang with several thousand light boats to fight upstream; Zhang Huishao and others attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，東昏侯以豫州刺史陳伯之為江州刺史、假節、都督前鋒諸軍事，西擊荊、雍。

translations.literal: On guichou Marquis Donghun made Governor of Yuzhou Chen Bozhi Governor of Jiangzhou with acting credentials and Director of All Vanguard Forces, to strike west against Jing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Marquis Donghun appointed Chen Bozhi, Governor of Yu Province, Governor of Jiang Province with acting credentials and supreme commander of the vanguard, to strike west against Jing and Yong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，蕭衍出沔，命王茂、蕭穎達等進軍逼郢城，薛元嗣不敢出。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Xiao Yan advanced along the Mian, ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and others to advance and press Ying city; Xue Yuansi did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Xiao Yan advanced along the Mian River and ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and others to press Ying city. Xue Yuansi did not dare come out.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲攻之，衍不許。

translations.literal: The generals wished to assault it; Yan did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wished to assault the city, but Yan would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 魏廣陵惠王羽通於員外郎馮俊興妻，夜往，為俊興所擊而匿之；

translations.literal: The Northern Wei Prince of Guangling, Yuan Yu, had an affair with the wife of the Supplementary Gentleman Feng Junxing; he went by night and was struck by Junxing and hid;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Yu of Guangling of Northern Wei had an affair with the wife of Supplementary Gentleman Feng Junxing. Yu went to her by night, was struck by Junxing, and went into hiding;

sentences.zh: 五月，壬子，卒。

translations.literal: Fifth month, renzi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renzi, he died.

sentences.zh: 魏主既親政事，嬖倖擅權，王公希得進見。

translations.literal: Once the Wei emperor personally handled government, favorites monopolized power, and kings and dukes rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Wei emperor took up government in person, favorites monopolized power, and princes and grandees rarely gained audience.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧意不自安，齋帥劉小苟屢言於禧雲，聞天子左右人言欲誅禧。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Xianyang felt ill at ease; Fast-Master Liu Xiaogou repeatedly told Xi that he had heard people close to the Son of Heaven say they wished to execute Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang grew uneasy. Fast-Master Liu Xiaogou repeatedly told Xi that he had heard those close to the emperor speak of executing him.

sentences.zh: 禧益懼，乃與妃兄兼給事黃門侍郎李伯尚、氐王楊集始、楊靈祏、乞伏馬居等謀反。

translations.literal: Xi grew more fearful and thereupon plotted rebellion with his consort's brother, Concurrent Attendant of Affairs and Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Boshang, Di king Yang Jishi, Yang Lingyou, and Qifu Maju and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xi grew more fearful and plotted rebellion with his consort's brother Li Boshang, Concurrent Attendant of Affairs and Yellow Gate Gentleman, the Di king Yang Jishi, Yang Lingyou, Qifu Maju, and others.

sentences.zh: 會帝出獵北邙，禧與其黨會城西小宅，欲發兵襲帝，使長子通竊入河內舉兵相應。

translations.literal: When the emperor went out to hunt at Beimang, Xi met his faction at a small house west of the city, intending to raise troops to strike the emperor and send his eldest son Tong secretly into Henei to raise forces in response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went hunting at Beimang, Xi met his faction at a small house west of the city, intending to raise troops to strike the emperor and send his eldest son Tong secretly into Henei to raise forces in support.

sentences.zh: 乞伏馬居說禧：「還入洛城，勒門閉門，天子必北走桑干，殿下可斷河橋，為河南天子。

translations.literal: Qifu Maju urged Xi: "Return into Luoyang, shut the gates, the Son of Heaven is sure to flee north to Sanggan—Your Highness can cut the river bridge and become Son of Heaven south of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Maju urged Xi, "Return into Luoyang and shut the gates. The emperor is sure to flee north to the Sanggan River. Your Highness can cut the river bridge and become emperor south of the river."

sentences.zh: 」眾情前卻不壹，禧心更緩，自旦至晡，猶豫不決，遂約不洩而散。

translations.literal: The group's sentiments advanced and retreated without unity; Xi's heart grew slower still. From dawn to dusk he hesitated without decision, and finally agreed not to leak the plot and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators' resolve wavered back and forth. Xi's heart grew slower still. From dawn to dusk he hesitated without deciding, and finally they agreed to keep the plot secret and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 楊集始既出，即馳至北邙告之。

translations.literal: Once Yang Jishi had left, he immediately galloped to Beimang to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Jishi had left, he galloped straight to Beimang to inform on the plot.

sentences.zh: 直寢苻承祖、薛魏孫與禧通謀，是日，帝寢於浮圖之陰，魏孫欲弒帝，承祖曰：「吾聞殺天者身當病癩。

translations.literal: Direct Attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun were in league with Xi's plot; that day the emperor slept in the shade of a pagoda. Weisun wished to assassinate the emperor; Chengzu said: "I have heard that one who kills Heaven's Son will himself contract leprosy."
translations.idiomatic: Direct Attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun were party to Xi's conspiracy. That day the emperor slept in the shade of a pagoda. Weisun wished to assassinate him, but Chengzu said, "I have heard that whoever kills the Son of Heaven will himself contract leprosy."

sentences.zh: 」魏孫乃止。

translations.literal: Weisun thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Weisun thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝寤，集始亦至。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor awoke, and Jishi also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the emperor woke, and Jishi arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 帝左右皆四出逐禽，直衛無幾，倉猝不知所出。

translations.literal: The emperor's attendants had all gone out in four directions to chase game; direct guards were few; in haste none knew what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's attendants had all scattered in pursuit of game; only a handful of guards remained, and in the sudden alarm no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將於忠曰：「臣父領軍留守京城，計防遏有備，必無所慮。

translations.literal: Left Palace Gentleman Yu Zhong said: "Your servant's father commands the army on garrison in the capital; I reckon that prevention and containment are in readiness—there is surely nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Left Palace Gentleman Yu Zhong said, "My father holds the capital with the army. Defenses are already in place—there is nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 」帝遣忠馳騎觀之，於烈已分兵嚴備，使忠還奏曰：「臣雖老，心力猶可用。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent Zhong galloping on horseback to observe; Yu Lie had already divided troops and made strict preparations, and had Zhong return to report, saying: "Though your servant is old, mind and strength may still be used.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Zhong galloping to look. Yu Lie had already divided his forces and made strict preparations, and sent Zhong back to report, "I am old, but my wits and strength still serve.

sentences.zh: 此屬猖狂，不足為慮，願陛下清蹕徐還，以安物望。

translations.literal: This lot are wildly arrogant, not worth anxiety; I wish Your Majesty to clear the way and return slowly to settle the expectations of the world.
translations.idiomatic: This rabble is reckless and not worth a thought. May Your Majesty return at ease with escort cleared to steady court and people alike.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅，自華林園還宮，撫於忠之背曰：「卿差強人意！

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased; from Hualin Garden he returned to the palace and stroked Yu Zhong's back, saying: "You are rather more satisfactory than one might expect!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased. He returned from Hualin Garden to the palace and patted Yu Zhong on the back. "You are rather more satisfactory than one might expect!"

sentences.zh: 禧不知事露，與姬妾及左右宿洪池別墅，遣劉小苟奉啟，雲檢行田收。

translations.literal: Xi did not know the affair had been exposed; he lodged with concubines and attendants at the Hongchi estate and sent Liu Xiaogou to present a memorial, saying he was inspecting field harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Xi did not know the plot had been exposed. He stayed with his concubines and attendants at the Hongchi villa and sent Liu Xiaogou with a memorial claiming he was out inspecting the harvest.

sentences.zh: 小苟至北邙，已逢軍人，怪小苟赤衣，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Xiaogou reached Northern Mang, already encountered soldiers; they thought Xiaogou's red garb strange and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogou reached Northern Mang he ran into troops. They thought his red clothing odd and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 小苟困迫，言欲告反，乃緩之。

translations.literal: Xiaogou, cornered, said he wished to report rebellion, and they then relaxed their hold.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Xiaogou said he had come to report a rebellion, and they spared him.

sentences.zh: 或謂禧曰：「殿下集眾圖事，見意而停，恐必漏洩，今夕何宜自寬！

translations.literal: Someone told Xi: "Your Highness gathered a crowd to plot the affair; once the intent was seen you halted—I fear it must leak; how can tonight be a time for ease!
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Xi, "Your Highness gathered men to plot, then stopped when the plan was noticed. It will surely leak out—how can you relax tonight!"

sentences.zh: 」禧曰：「吾有此身，應知自惜，豈待人言！

translations.literal: " Xi said: "I have this body of mine; I ought to know to cherish it—why wait for others' words!
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said, "I have my life to look after. I know how to take care of myself—why wait for others to tell me!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「殿下長子已濟河，兩不相知，豈不可慮！

translations.literal: " Another said: "Your Highness's eldest son has already crossed the river; neither knows the other's situation—how can that not cause concern!
translations.idiomatic: " Another said, "Your Highness's eldest son has already crossed the river. Neither side knows what the other is doing—is that not worrying!"

sentences.zh: 」禧曰：「吾已遣人追之，計今應還。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "I have already sent men to pursue him; I reckon by now he ought to have returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said, "I have already sent men after him. By now he should be back."

sentences.zh: 」時通已入河內，列兵仗，放囚徒矣。

translations.literal: " By then Tong had already entered Henei, arrayed weapons, and released prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Tong had already entered Henei, drawn up arms, and released prisoners.

sentences.zh: 於烈遣直閣叔孫侯將虎賁三百人收禧。

translations.literal: Yu Lie sent Direct Attendant Sunsun Hou leading three hundred tiger guards to take Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lie sent Direct Attendant Sunsun Hou with three hundred tiger guards to seize Xi.

sentences.zh: 禧聞之，自洪池東南走，僮僕不過數人，濟洛，至柏谷塢，追兵至，擒之，送華林都亭。

translations.literal: Xi heard it; from Hongchi he fled southeast, retainers numbering no more than a few; he crossed the Luo, reaching the Bo Valley stockade; pursuers arrived, seized him, and sent him to the Hualin metropolitan pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi heard this he fled southeast from Hongchi with only a few servants, crossed the Luo, and reached the Bo Valley stockade. Pursuers caught up, seized him, and sent him to the Hualin metropolitan pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝面詰其反狀，壬戌，賜死於私第。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated him face to face on his rebellion; on renxu, he was granted death in his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him to his face about the rebellion. On renxu he was granted death in his private residence.

sentences.zh: 同謀伏誅者十餘人，諸子皆絕屬籍，微給貲產、奴婢，自餘家財悉分賜高肇及趙修之家，其餘賜內外百官，逮於流外，多者百餘匹，下至十匹。

translations.literal: More than ten co-conspirators were executed; all sons were struck from the clan register, given meager property and slaves; the rest of the household wealth was all divided and bestowed on the households of Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the remainder was bestowed on inner and outer officials, reaching even to distant exile—some received more than a hundred bolts, down to ten bolts.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten co-conspirators were executed. All his sons were struck from the clan register and given only a pittance in goods and slaves. The rest of the family wealth was divided between the households of Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the remainder went to officials inside and outside the court, even those in distant exile—some received more than a hundred bolts of cloth, others as few as ten.

sentences.zh: 禧諸子乏衣食，獨彭城王屢賑給之。

translations.literal: Xi's sons lacked food and clothing; only the Prince of Pengcheng repeatedly relief-supplied them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's sons lacked food and clothing; only the Prince of Pengcheng repeatedly provided for them.

sentences.zh: 河內太守陸琇聞禧敗，斬送禧子通首。

translations.literal: Henei Administrator Lu Xiu heard of Xi's defeat, beheaded and sent Tong's head.
translations.idiomatic: Henei Administrator Lu Xiu, hearing of Xi's defeat, beheaded Xi's son Tong and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 魏朝以琇於禧未敗之前不收捕通，責其通情，征詣廷尉，死獄中。

translations.literal: The Wei court, because Xiu before Xi's defeat had not arrested and seized Tong, charged him with collusion; he was summoned to the Minister of Justice and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court faulted Xiu for not arresting Tong before Xi's defeat, charged him with collusion, summoned him to the Minister of Justice, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 帝以禧無故而反，由是益疏忌宗室。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xi had rebelled without cause, from this grew still more distant and suspicious toward the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi had rebelled without apparent cause, the emperor grew still more distant and suspicious toward the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 巴西太守魯休烈、巴東太守蕭惠訓不從蕭穎冑之命；

translations.literal: Administrator of Baxi Lu Xiulie and Administrator of Badong Xiao Huixun did not follow Xiao Yinghao's orders;
translations.idiomatic: The administrators of Baxi, Lu Xiulie, and of Badong, Xiao Huixun, did not obey Xiao Yinghao's orders;

sentences.zh: 惠訓遣子瑰將兵擊穎冑，穎冑，遣汶陽太守劉孝慶屯峽口，與巴東太守任漾之等拒之。

translations.literal: Huixun sent his son Gui leading troops to attack Yinghao; Yinghao sent Administrator of Wenyang Liu Xiaoqing to encamp at Xia Pass, and with Administrator of Badong Ren Yangzhi and others to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Huixun sent his son Gui with troops to attack Yinghao. Yinghao sent the administrator of Wenyang, Liu Xiaoqing, to hold Xia Pass, and with the administrator of Badong, Ren Yangzhi, and others to resist him.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯遣軍主吳子陽、陳虎牙等十三軍救郢州，進屯巴口。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness sent Army Commanders Wu Ziyang, Chen Huya, and thirteen armies to relieve Ying Province, advancing to encamp at Bakou.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness sent army commanders Wu Ziyang and Chen Huya with thirteen armies to relieve Ying Province, advancing to encamp at Bakou.

sentences.zh: 虎牙，伯之之子也。

translations.literal: Huya was Bozhi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Huya was the son of Chen Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 六月，西台遣衛尉席闡文勞蕭衍軍，繼蕭穎冑等議謂衍曰：「今頓兵兩岸，不並軍圍郢，定西陽、武昌，取江州，此機已失；

translations.literal: Sixth month; the Western Terrace sent Chamberlain Xi Kanwen to comfort Xiao Yan's army; following Xiao Yinghao and others, they deliberated and told Yan: "Now troops are halted on both banks, yet armies are not united to besiege Ying, to secure Xiyang and Wuchang, and take Jiang Province—this opportunity is already lost;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Western Terrace sent Chamberlain Xi Kanwen to visit Xiao Yan's army. Following Xiao Yinghao and the others, they advised Yan, "You have troops on both banks of the river but have not united them to besiege Ying, secure Xiyang and Wuchang, and take Jiang Province. That chance is already gone;

sentences.zh: 莫若請救於魏，與北連和，猶為上策。

translations.literal: better to seek rescue from Wei and join in alliance with the north—this would still be the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: better to seek aid from Wei and ally with the north. That would still be the best plan.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「漢口路通荊、雍，控引秦、梁，糧運資儲，仰引氣息；

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Hankou's roads connect Jing and Yong, control and draw Qin and Liang; grain transport and supplies depend on it for breath;
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "Hankou links Jing and Yong and commands Qin and Liang. Grain and supplies depend on it for our very breath;

sentences.zh: 所以兵壓漢口，連結數州。

translations.literal: therefore troops press Hankou and link several provinces.
translations.idiomatic: that is why we press Hankou with our army and hold several provinces together.

sentences.zh: 今若並軍圍郢，又分兵前進，魯山必阻沔路，扼吾咽喉；

translations.literal: Now if armies are united to besiege Ying while also dividing troops to advance, Mount Lu will surely block the Mian route and choke our throat;
translations.idiomatic: If we unite to besiege Ying while also sending troops forward, Mount Lu will block the Mian route and choke our throat;

sentences.zh: 若糧運不通，自然離散，何謂持久？

translations.literal: if grain transport is cut, men will naturally scatter—what is called endurance?
translations.idiomatic: once grain cannot get through, the army will scatter on its own. What endurance is there in that?

sentences.zh: 鄧元起近欲以三千兵往取尋陽，彼若歡然知機，一說士足矣；

translations.literal: Deng Yuanqi of late wishes to take Xunyang with three thousand troops; if they gladly grasp the moment, one persuader is enough;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanqi lately wanted to take Xunyang with three thousand men. If they gladly seize the moment, one envoy is enough;

sentences.zh: 脫距王師，固非三千兵所能下也。

translations.literal: if they resist the royal army, it is surely not something three thousand troops can take.
translations.idiomatic: but if they resist the royal army, three thousand men will never take it.

sentences.zh: 進退無據，未見其可。

translations.literal: Advance and retreat without footing—I do not see how it can work.
translations.idiomatic: With no firm footing for advance or retreat, I do not see how it can succeed.

sentences.zh: 西陽、武昌，取之即得；

translations.literal: Xiyang and Wuchang—take them and they are won;
translations.idiomatic: Xiyang and Wuchang can be taken at once;

sentences.zh: 然既得之後，即應鎮守。

translations.literal: yet once obtained, one must immediately garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: but once taken they must be garrisoned at once.

sentences.zh: 欲守兩城，不減萬人，糧儲稱是，卒無所出。

translations.literal: To hold two cities requires no fewer than ten thousand men, and commensurate grain stores—soldiers have nowhere to come from.
translations.idiomatic: Holding two cities takes no fewer than ten thousand men and matching stores of grain, and we have no troops to spare.

sentences.zh: 脫東軍有上者，以萬人攻一城，兩城勢不得相救，若我分軍應援，則首尾俱弱；

translations.literal: If eastern forces attack, ten thousand men against one city—the two cities by circumstance cannot rescue each other; if we divide armies to reinforce, then head and tail are both weak;
translations.idiomatic: If the eastern army attacks, ten thousand men can take one city. The two cities cannot rescue each other. If we split our forces to help, head and tail grow weak together;

sentences.zh: 如其不遣，孤城必陷，一城既沒，諸城相次土崩，天下大事去矣。

translations.literal: if we do not send troops, isolated cities will surely fall; once one city is lost, other cities will collapse in succession—the great affair of the realm is gone.
translations.idiomatic: if we do not send help, each lone city will fall. Once one is lost, the rest will crumble in turn, and the great enterprise is finished.

sentences.zh: 若郢州既拔，席捲沿流，西陽、武昌自然風靡。

translations.literal: If Ying Province is already taken, sweeping along the current, Xiyang and Wuchang will naturally bow to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ying Province falls, we can sweep down the river and Xiyang and Wuchang will submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 何遽分兵散眾，自貽憂患乎！

translations.literal: Why hastily divide troops and scatter the host, bringing trouble on oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Why hurry to divide the army and scatter our strength, bringing trouble on ourselves!

sentences.zh: 且丈夫舉事欲清天步，況擁數州之兵以誅群小，懸河注火，奚有不滅！

translations.literal: Moreover a man undertaking great affairs wishes to cleanse the steps of Heaven; how much more with troops of several provinces to punish petty fellows—pouring a river to extinguish fire, what would not be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: A man who takes up great affairs means to set Heaven's steps in order. How much more when we hold several provinces' worth of troops to punish petty foes—pour a river on a fire, and what will not be put out!

sentences.zh: 豈容北面請救戎狄，以示弱於天下！

translations.literal: How can one turn north to beg barbarian rescue, showing weakness to all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: How can we turn north to beg barbarians for rescue and show weakness to the world!

sentences.zh: 彼未必能信，徒取丑聲，此乃下計，何謂上策！

translations.literal: They may not necessarily trust us, only gaining ugly renown—this is the inferior plan; how is it called the superior stratagem!
translations.idiomatic: They may not even trust us, and we would only earn a shameful name. That is the low plan—how can you call it the high one!

sentences.zh: 卿為我輩白鎮軍：「前途攻取，但以見付，事在目中，無患不捷，但借鎮軍靖鎮之耳。

translations.literal: You speak for us to the Commander-in-Chief: "Future attacks and seizures—just leave them to us; the affair is before our eyes; no worry of failure—only lend the Commander-in-Chief's tranquil garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Commander-in-Chief for us: "Leave the fighting ahead to us. The matter is before our eyes and cannot fail to succeed. We only ask that he hold the rear in quiet."

sentences.zh: 吳子陽等進軍武口。

translations.literal: Wu Ziyang and others advanced army to Wukou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ziyang and the others advanced on Wukou.

sentences.zh: 衍命軍主梁天惠等屯漁湖城，唐修期等屯白陽壘，夾岸待之。

translations.literal: Yan ordered Army Commanders Liang Tianhui and others to encamp at Yuhu Citadel, Tang Xiuqi and others at Baiyang Rampart, waiting on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered army commanders Liang Tianhui and others to hold Yuhu Citadel and Tang Xiuqi and others to hold Baiyang Rampart, waiting on both banks.

sentences.zh: 子陽進軍加湖，去郢三十里，傍山帶水，築壘自固。

translations.literal: Ziyang advanced army to Jia Lake, thirty li from Ying, along mountain and water building ramparts to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyang advanced to Jia Lake, thirty li from Ying, and along the hills and water built ramparts to fortify himself.

sentences.zh: 子陽舉烽，城內亦舉火應之；

translations.literal: Ziyang raised beacon fires; within the city fires were also raised in response;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyang raised beacon fires, and within the city answering fires were lit;

sentences.zh: 而內外各自保，不能相救。

translations.literal: yet inner and outer each held to themselves and could not rescue each other.
translations.idiomatic: but inner and outer each held their own ground and could not help one another.

sentences.zh: 會房僧寄病卒，眾復推助防張樂祖代守魯山。

translations.literal: When Fang Sengji died of illness, the host again pushed Assistant Defense Commander Zhang Lezu to replace guarding Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Sengji died of illness, the troops again chose Assistant Defense Commander Zhang Lezu to take over the defense of Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎冑之初起也，弟穎孚自建康發，廬陵民修靈祏為之聚兵，得二千人，襲房陵，克之，內史謝篹奔豫章。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yinghao first rose, his younger brother Yingfu set out from Jiankang; Luling native Xiu Lingyou gathered troops for him, obtaining two thousand men; they raided Fangling and took it; Interior Minister Xie Zan fled to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yinghao first rose, his younger brother Yingfu set out from Jiankang. The Luling man Xiu Lingyou raised troops for him, mustering two thousand men. They raided Fangling and took it, and Interior Minister Xie Zan fled to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 穎冑遣寧朔將軍范僧簡自湘州赴之，僧簡拔安成，穎冑以僧簡為安成太守，以穎孚為廬陵內史。

translations.literal: Yinghao sent Bulwark General Fan Jianjian from Xiang Province to go to his aid; Jianjian took Ancheng; Yinghao appointed Jianjian Administrator of Ancheng and Yingfu Interior Minister of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Yinghao sent Bulwark General Fan Jianjian from Xiang Province to his aid. Jianjian took Ancheng. Yinghao made Jianjian administrator of Ancheng and Yingfu interior minister of Luling.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯遣軍主劉希祖將三千人擊之，南康太守王丹以郡應希祖。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness sent Army Commander Liu Xizu leading three thousand men to attack them; Administrator of Nankang Wang Dan brought the commandery to join Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness sent army commander Liu Xizu with three thousand men to attack them. The administrator of Nankang, Wang Dan, brought his commandery over to Xizu.

sentences.zh: 穎孚敗，奔長沙，尋病卒；

translations.literal: Yingfu was defeated, fled to Changsha, and soon died of illness;
translations.idiomatic: Yingfu was defeated, fled to Changsha, and soon died of illness;

sentences.zh: 謝篹復還郡。

translations.literal: Xie Zan returned again to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zan returned to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 希祖攻拔安成，殺范僧簡，東昏侯以希祖為安成內史。

translations.literal: Xizu attacked and took Ancheng, killed Fan Jianjian; the Marquis of Eastern Benightedness made Xizu Interior Minister of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xizu attacked and took Ancheng and killed Fan Jianjian. The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness made Xizu interior minister of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 修靈祏復合餘眾攻謝篹，篹敗走。

translations.literal: Xiu Lingyou again gathered remnant troops to attack Xie Zan; Zan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Lingyou gathered his remaining troops again and attacked Xie Zan. Zan was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯作芳樂苑，山石皆塗以五采。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness built the Fragrant Pleasure Park; mountain rocks were all painted in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Eastern Benightedness built the Fragrant Pleasure Park and painted the mountain rocks in five colors.

sentences.zh: 望民家有好樹、美竹，則毀牆撤屋而徙之，時方盛暑，隨即枯萎，朝暮相繼。

translations.literal: Seeing common households with fine trees and beautiful bamboo, he tore down walls and removed houses to transplant them; it was then the height of summer and they withered at once—morning and evening in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw fine trees or beautiful bamboo in people's homes, he tore down walls and houses to transplant them. It was high summer, and they withered at once—one after another, morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 又於苑中立市，使宮人、宦者共為裨販，以潘貴妃為市令，東昏侯自為市錄事，小有得失，妃則與杖；

translations.literal: Moreover within the park he established a market, making palace women and eunuchs together act as peddlers; Consort Pan Guifei was market magistrate; the Marquis himself was market recorder; for slight gains and losses the consort would supply the beating;
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a market in the park where palace women and eunuchs played peddlers. Consort Pan Guifei was market magistrate and the Marquis himself market recorder. For the slightest gain or loss the consort would beat him;

sentences.zh: 乃敕虎賁不得進大荊、實中荻。

translations.literal: he then commanded tiger guards not to bring large thorn switches or solid-center rattan.
translations.idiomatic: he then ordered the tiger guards not to bring large thorn switches or solid-center rattan rods.

sentences.zh: 又開渠立埭，身自引船，或坐而屠肉。

translations.literal: He also opened canals and built weirs, personally towing boats, or sitting to butcher meat.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug canals and built weirs, towing boats himself or sitting down to butcher meat.

sentences.zh: 又好巫覡，左右朱光尚詐雲見鬼。

translations.literal: He also loved shamans and spirit-mediums; his attendant Zhu Guangshang fraudulently said he saw ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved shamans and mediums. His attendant Zhu Guangshang pretended that he saw ghosts.

sentences.zh: 東昏入樂游苑，人馬忽驚，以問光尚，對曰：「向見先帝大嗔，不許數出。

translations.literal: The Marquis entered Leyou Park; men and horses suddenly startled; he questioned Guangshang, who replied: "Just now I saw the late emperor greatly angry, not permitting frequent outings.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis entered Leyou Park and men and horses suddenly panicked. He asked Guangshang, who answered, "I just saw the late emperor very angry, forbidding you to go out so often."

sentences.zh: 」東昏大怒，拔刀與光尚尋之。

translations.literal: " The Marquis was greatly enraged, drew a sword and with Guangshang searched for him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Marquis flew into a rage, drew his sword, and went with Guangshang to hunt for him.

sentences.zh: 既不見，乃縛菰為高宗形，北向斬之，縣首苑門。

translations.literal: Finding nothing, he bound rush into the form of Emperor Gaozong, beheaded it facing north, and hung the head at the park gate.
translations.idiomatic: Finding nothing, he bound rushes into the shape of Emperor Gaozong, beheaded the effigy facing north, and hung the head at the park gate.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景之敗也，巴陵王昭冑、永新侯昭穎出投台軍，各以王侯還第，心不自安。

translations.literal: At Cui Huijing's defeat, Prince of Baling Zhao Zhao and Marquis of Yongxin Zhao Ying went out to join the capital armies; each returned to residence as king and marquis, hearts not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's defeat, Prince Zhao of Baling and Marquis Zhao of Yongxin went over to the capital armies. Each returned to his residence as king or marquis, but neither felt secure.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良故防閣桑偃為梅蟲兒軍副，與前巴西太守蕭寅謀立昭冑，昭冑許事克用寅為尚書左僕射、護軍。

translations.literal: Former guard-chamberlain of Prince Ziliang of Jingling Sang Yan served as deputy to Mei Chong'er's army; with former Administrator of Baxi Xiao Yin he plotted to enthrone Zhao Zhao; Zhao promised if the affair succeeded to employ Yin as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Director of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yan, former guard-chamberlain of Prince Ziliang of Jingling, served as Mei Chong'er's army deputy. With the former administrator of Baxi, Xiao Yin, he plotted to enthrone Zhao. Zhao promised that if the plot succeeded he would make Yin Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Director of Guards.

sentences.zh: 時軍主胡松將兵屯新亭，寅遣人說之曰：「須昏人出，寅等將兵奉昭冑入台，閉城號令，昏人必還就將軍；

translations.literal: Then Army Commander Hu Song was encamped at Xinting; Yin sent someone to persuade him: "We must wait for the Benighted One to go out; Yin and others will lead troops to escort Zhao into the Terrace, close the city and issue orders—the Benighted One will surely return to join the general;
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Hu Song was then encamped at Xinting. Yin sent someone to persuade him, "Wait until the Benighted One goes out. Yin and the rest will lead troops to escort Zhao into the Terrace, close the city, and issue orders. The Benighted One will surely return to you;

sentences.zh: 但閉壘不應，，則三公不足得也。

translations.literal: only close the ramparts and do not respond—then the Three Excellencies cannot be reached."
translations.idiomatic: only close your ramparts and do not respond, and the Three Excellencies cannot be touched."

sentences.zh: 」松許諾。

translations.literal: " Song promised assent.
translations.idiomatic: " Song agreed.

sentences.zh: 會東昏新作芳樂苑，經月不出遊。

translations.literal: As it happened the Marquis of Eastern Benightedness had newly built the Fragrant Pleasure Park and for a month did not go out roaming.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened the Marquis had just built the Fragrant Pleasure Park and for a month did not go out.

sentences.zh: 偃等議募健兒百餘人，從萬春門入，突取之，昭冑以為不可。

translations.literal: Yan and others deliberated recruiting stalwart youths of more than a hundred to enter through Wanchun Gate and seize him suddenly; Zhao thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the others planned to recruit more than a hundred stalwart youths to enter through Wanchun Gate and seize him by surprise. Zhao thought it would not do.

sentences.zh: 偃同黨王山沙慮事久無成，以事告御刀徐僧重。

translations.literal: Yan's partisan Wang Shansha, fearing the affair long without success, reported the matter to Imperial Blade Xu Chongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's confederate Wang Shansha, fearing the plot would never succeed, reported it to Imperial Blade Xu Chongzhong.

sentences.zh: 寅遣人殺山沙於路，吏於麝幐得其事。

translations.literal: Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road; officials in a musk pouch obtained the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road, but officials found the plot described in a musk pouch.

sentences.zh: 昭冑兄弟與偃等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao's brothers and Yan and others all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's brothers and Yan and the rest were all executed.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史張欣泰與弟前始安內史欣時，密謀結胡松及前南譙太守王靈秀、直閣將軍鴻選等誅諸嬖倖，廢東昏。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yong Province Zhang Xintai and his younger brother, former Interior Minister of Shian Xinshi, secretly plotted to join Hu Song and former Administrator of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, Direct Attendant Hong Xuan and others to execute the favorites and depose the Marquis of Eastern Benightedness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xintai, inspector of Yong Province, and his younger brother Xinshi, former interior minister of Shian, secretly plotted with Hu Song, the former administrator of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, Direct Attendant Hong Xuan, and others to kill the favorites and depose the Marquis of Eastern Benightedness.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣中書舍人馮元嗣監軍救郢；

translations.literal: The Marquis sent Palace Gentleman Feng Yuansi to supervise the army relieving Ying;
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis sent Palace Gentleman Feng Yuansi to supervise the army relieving Ying;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，茹法珍、梅蟲兒及太子右率李居士、制局監楊明泰送之於中興堂，欣泰等使人懷刀於座斫元嗣，頭墜果柈中，又斫明泰，破其腹；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jiawu; Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard Li Jushi, Control Bureau Supervisor Yang Mingtai escorted him to Zhongxing Hall; Xintai and others had men conceal blades at their seats to hack YuanSi—head fell into the fruit tray; they also hacked Mingtai, splitting his belly;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard Li Jushi, and Control Bureau Supervisor Yang Mingtai escorted him to Zhongxing Hall. Xintai and the others had men hide blades at their seats and strike YuanSi. His head fell into the fruit tray. They also struck Mingtai and split open his belly;

sentences.zh: 蟲兒傷數瘡，手指皆墮；

translations.literal: Chong'er suffered several wounds, all fingers falling off;
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er took several wounds and all his fingers were cut off;

sentences.zh: 居士、法珍等散走還台。

translations.literal: Jushi, Fazhen and others scattered and fled back to the Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi, Fazhen, and the others scattered and fled back to the Terrace.

sentences.zh: 靈秀詣石頭迎建康王寶寅，帥城中將吏見力，去車輪，載寶寅，文武數百唱警蹕，向台城，百姓數千人皆空手隨之。

translations.literal: Lingxiu went to Stone City to welcome Prince of Jiankang Bao Yin, leading within the city military officers according to their strength, removed carriage wheels, loaded Yin, several hundred civil and military chanting guard-clearing, toward the Terrace City, several thousand commoners all empty-handed following.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu went to Stone City to welcome Prince Bao of Jiankang, leading such officers and men as the city could muster. They removed the carriage wheels, loaded Bao Yin aboard, and several hundred civil and military officials cried the guard-clearing chant as they marched on the Terrace City. Several thousand commoners followed empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 欣泰聞事作，馳馬入宮，冀法珍等在外，東昏盡以城中處分見委，表裡相應。

translations.literal: Xintai heard the affair had begun, galloped into the palace, hoping Fazhen and others were outside, the Marquis would wholly entrust disposition of the city to him, inner and outer corresponding.
translations.idiomatic: When Xintai heard the plot had begun he galloped into the palace, hoping Fazhen and the others were still outside and that the Marquis would entrust the whole city to him so inner and outer could act together.

sentences.zh: 既而法珍得返，處分閉門上仗，不配欣泰兵，鴻選在殿內亦不敢發。

translations.literal: Before long Fazhen returned, directed closing gates and mounting arms, not assigning troops to Xintai; Hong Xuan within the hall also did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: But Fazhen soon returned, ordered the gates shut and arms mounted, and gave Xintai no troops. Hong Xuan inside the hall also did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 寶寅去杜姥宅，日已瞑，城門閉。

translations.literal: Yin left Old Lady Du's residence; the sun had already set; city gates were closed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yin left Old Lady Du's house. The sun had set and the city gates were closed.

sentences.zh: 城上人射外人，外人棄寶寅潰去。

translations.literal: Men atop the wall shot outsiders; outsiders abandoned Yin and routed away.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the wall shot at those outside, and the crowd abandoned Bao Yin and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 寶寅亦逃，三日，乃戎服詣草市尉，尉馳以啟東昏。

translations.literal: Yin also fled; on the third day he donned military garb and went to the Grass Market Commandant; the commandant galloped to report to the Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yin also fled. On the third day he put on military dress and went to the Grass Market Commandant, who galloped to report to the Marquis.

sentences.zh: 東昏召寶寅入宮問之，寶寅涕泣稱：「爾日不知何人逼使上車，仍將去，制不自由。

translations.literal: The Marquis summoned Yin into the palace to question him; Yin weeping said: "That day I did not know who forced me into the carriage and took me away—I was not free to control myself.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis summoned Bao Yin into the palace to question him. Bao Yin wept and said, "That day I did not know who forced me into a carriage and took me away. I was not free to act."

sentences.zh: 」東昏笑，復其爵位。

translations.literal: " The Marquis laughed and restored his titles.
translations.idiomatic: " The Marquis laughed and restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 張欣泰等事覺，與胡松皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Xintai and others' affair was exposed; he and Hu Song were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xintai's plot was exposed, he and Hu Song were both executed.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍使征虜將軍王茂、軍主曹仲宗等乘水漲以舟師襲加湖，鼓噪攻之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent Campaigning General Wang Mao and Army Commander Cao Zhongzong and others, riding the flood's rise with a fleet to strike Jia Lake, drumming and shouting in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Campaigning General Wang Mao and army commander Cao Zhongzong and others to take advantage of the rising waters and attack Jia Lake with a fleet, drumming and shouting as they assaulted it.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加湖潰，吳子陽等走免，將士殺溺死者萬計，俘其餘眾而還。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Jia Lake collapsed; Wu Ziyang and others fled and escaped; soldiers killed and drowned numbered in the tens of thousands; they captured the remainder and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the camp at Jia Lake collapsed. Wu Ziyang and the others fled. Tens of thousands of their men were killed or drowned, and the rest were taken prisoner before the army returned.

sentences.zh: 於是郢、魯二城相視奪氣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two cities of Ying and Lu looked at each other and lost spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the garrisons at Ying and Mount Lu lost heart when they looked at one another.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，柔然犯魏邊。

translations.literal: On yisi, Rouran invaded the Wei frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Rouran invaded the Wei frontier.

sentences.zh: 魯山乏糧，軍人於磯頭捕細魚供食，密治輕船，將奔夏口，蕭衍遣偏軍斷其走路。

translations.literal: Mount Lu lacked grain; soldiers at Jitou caught small fish for food, secretly preparing light boats intending to flee to Xiakou; Xiao Yan sent a detached force to cut their escape route.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Lu ran short of grain. The soldiers caught small fish at Jitou to eat and secretly built light boats, intending to flee to Xiakou. Xiao Yan sent a detached force to cut off their escape.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，孫樂祖窘迫，以城降。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Sun Lezu, cornered, surrendered the city with citadel.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Sun Lezu, hard pressed, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 己未，東昏侯以程茂為郢州刺史，薛元嗣為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Marquis Donghun appointed Cheng Mao Governor of Ying Province and Xue Yuansi Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Marquis Donghun appointed Cheng Mao governor of Ying Province and Xue Yuansi governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 是日，茂、元嗣以郢城降。

translations.literal: That same day, Mao and Yuansi surrendered Ying City.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Mao and Yuansi surrendered Ying City.

sentences.zh: 郢城之初圍也，士民男女近十萬口；

translations.literal: When Ying City was first besieged, the male and female populace numbered nearly one hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Ying City began, nearly a hundred thousand men, women, and children were trapped within;

sentences.zh: 閉門二百餘日，疾疫流腫，死者什七八，積屍床下而寢其上，比屋皆滿。

translations.literal: with gates shut for more than two hundred days, pestilence and running sores spread; seven or eight in ten died; corpses piled beneath the beds while they slept atop them, and every house was full.
translations.idiomatic: the gates stayed shut for more than two hundred days. Pestilence and festering sores swept the city; seven or eight in ten perished. Corpses heaped beneath the beds while the living slept above them, and house after house overflowed with the dead.

sentences.zh: 茂、元嗣等議出降，使張孜為書與衍。

translations.literal: Mao, Yuansi, and the rest deliberated surrendering the city and had Zhang Zi draft a letter to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, Yuansi, and their colleagues debated surrender and had Zhang Zi compose a letter to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 張沖故吏青州治中房長瑜謂孜曰：「前使君忠貫昊天，郎君但當坐守畫一荷析薪，若天運不與，當幅巾待命，下從使君。

translations.literal: Fang Changyu of Qing Province, Registrar and former subordinate of Zhang Chong, said to Zi: "The former governor's loyalty pierced the heavens; you, sir, need only sit firm and uphold a single policy and bear the burden of splitting firewood. If Heaven's mandate does not favor us, you should await orders in plain dress and follow the governor below.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Changyu, registrar of Qing Province and a former officer of Zhang Chong, told Zhang Zi: "Your father's loyalty reached to Heaven itself. You ought only to hold the line, keep one consistent policy, and shoulder the hard work of the cause. If fate turns against us, don the plain headcloth and wait for Heaven's word—then follow your father to the grave.

sentences.zh: 今從諸人之計，非唯郢州士女失高山之望，亦恐彼所不取也。

translations.literal: Now if you follow the others' plan, not only will the men and women of Ying Province lose their hopes set on a high mountain, but I fear even the enemy will not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: If you now adopt the crowd's counsel, you will not only dash the hopes Ying's people have pinned on you as on a mountain peak—you may find the enemy unwilling to accept you as well.

sentences.zh: 」孜不能用。

translations.literal: " Zi could not adopt his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zi would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍以韋睿為江夏太守，行郢府事，收瘞死者而無其生者，郢人遂安。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan appointed Wei Rui Administrator of Jiangxia to act in Ying prefectural affairs, buried the dead and relieved the living, and the people of Ying were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan made Wei Rui administrator of Jiangxia and acting prefect of Ying, buried the dead and succored the survivors, and the people of Ying at last found peace.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲頓軍夏口；

translations.literal: The generals wished to halt the army at Xiakou;
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to encamp at Xiakou;

sentences.zh: 衍以為宜乘勝直指建康，車騎咨議能軍張弘策、寧遠將軍庾域亦以為然。

translations.literal: Yan held that they should press their advantage and march straight on Jiankang; Zhang Hongce, Consulting Officer for Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of Able Troops, and Ningyuan General Yu Yu also thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued they should ride their victory straight to Jiankang; Zhang Hongce, consulting officer for the Chariots and Cavalry staff and commander of able troops, and the Ningyuan general Yu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 衍命眾軍即日上道。

translations.literal: Yan ordered the host to take the road that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered the entire army to march at once.

sentences.zh: 緣江至建康，凡磯、浦、村落，軍行宿次、立頓處所，弘策逆為圖畫，如在目中。

translations.literal: Following the river to Jiankang, every shoal, inlet, and hamlet—where the army camped, halted, and pitched—Hongce had drawn maps in advance, as though before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: All the way downriver toward Jiankang, for every shoal, creek mouth, and village—every campsite, halt, and staging ground along the line of march—Hongce had already charted the terrain in advance, as if it lay spread before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏安國宣簡侯王肅卒於壽陽，贈侍中、司空。

translations.literal: Wang Su, Marquis of Anguo, Xuanjian, of Wei, died at Shouyang; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, Marquis Xuanjian of Anguo in Wei, died at Shouyang and was posthumously honored as palace attendant and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，肅以父死非命，四年不除喪。

translations.literal: Earlier, because his father had died an unnatural death, Su observed mourning for four years without leaving it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because his father had died by violence, Wang Su had worn mourning for four years without ending it.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「三年之喪，賢者不敢過。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said: "The three-year mourning— even the worthy dare not exceed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "The three-year mourning—even the worthy dare not overstay it.

sentences.zh: 」命肅以祥禫之禮除喪。

translations.literal: " He ordered Su to leave mourning by the xiang and chan rites.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Wang Su to leave mourning with the xiang and chan ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 然肅猶素服、不聽樂終身。

translations.literal: Yet Su still wore plain dress and would not listen to music for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Su continued in plain dress and refused music for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 汝南民胡文超起兵於灄陽以應蕭衍，求取義陽、安陸等郡以自效；

translations.literal: Hu Wenchao, a man of Runan, raised troops at Zhenyang in response to Xiao Yan, seeking to take Yiyang, Anlu, and other commanderies to prove his merit;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wenchao of Runan raised an army at Zhenyang to join Xiao Yan, offering to seize Yiyang, Anlu, and neighboring commanderies in his service;

sentences.zh: 衍又遣軍主唐修期攻隨郡，皆克之。

translations.literal: Yan also sent the army commander Tang Xiuqi to attack Suicheng; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also sent the army commander Tang Xiuqi against Su commandery; all fell.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史王僧景遣子貞孫為質於衍，司部悉平。

translations.literal: Wang Jingjing, Governor of Si Province, sent his son Zhensun as hostage to Yan, and the Si region was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingjing, governor of Si Province, sent his son Zhensun as a hostage to Yan, and the whole Si region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景之死也，其少子偃為始安內史，逃潛得免。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing died, his youngest son Yan was Interior Secretary of Shi'an and, fleeing in hiding, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's death, his youngest son Yan, interior secretary of Shi'an, had hidden himself and survived.

sentences.zh: 及西台建，以偃為寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the Western Terrace was established, Yan was made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Terrace was set up, Yan was appointed general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 偃詣公車門上書曰：「臣竊惟高宗之孝子忠臣而昏主之亂臣賊子者，江夏王與陛下，先臣與鎮軍是也；

translations.literal: Yan went to the Gate of the Imperial Carriage and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant reflects that among Gaozong's filial sons and loyal ministers and among a benighted ruler's rebellious ministers and traitorous sons are the Prince of Jiangxia and Your Majesty, my late father and the Commander-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Yan went to the imperial carriage gate and submitted a memorial: "I reflect that among Emperor Gaozong's filial sons and loyal ministers—and among a benighted sovereign's rebellious ministers and traitorous sons—stand the Prince of Jiangxia and Your Majesty, my late father and the commander-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 雖成敗異術而所由同方。

translations.literal: though success and failure differ in method, the path they followed was the same.
translations.idiomatic: though fortune favored one side and not the other, they walked the same road.

sentences.zh: 陛下初登至尊，與天合符；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended the supreme seat and is in accord with Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly taken the throne and stands in harmony with Heaven;

sentences.zh: 天下纖介之屈，尚望陛下申之，況先帝之子陛下之兄，所行之道，即陛下所由哉！

translations.literal: even the slightest wrong under Heaven, your servant still hopes Your Majesty will redress it—how much more the late emperor's son, Your Majesty's elder brother, whose course was the very course Your Majesty has taken!
