translations.idiomatic: if even the smallest injustice in the realm may still hope for Your Majesty's redress, how much more the late emperor's son—Your Majesty's own elder brother—whose path was the very path Your Majesty has walked!

sentences.zh: 此尚弗恤，其餘何冀！

translations.literal: If this is still not pitied, what else may one hope for!
translations.idiomatic: If even this wins no pity, what hope remains for anything else!

sentences.zh: 今不可幸小民之無識而罔之；

translations.literal: Now one must not take advantage of the common people's want of understanding and deceive them;
translations.idiomatic: You must not gamble on the people's ignorance and mislead them;

sentences.zh: 若使曉然知其情節，相帥而逃，陛下將何以應之哉！

translations.literal: if they clearly knew the facts and led one another in flight, how would Your Majesty answer them!
translations.idiomatic: for if they came to know the truth and fled in a body, how would Your Majesty meet that!

sentences.zh: 」事寢，不報。

translations.literal: " The matter was shelved; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The petition was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 偃又上疏曰：「近冒陳江夏之兔，非敢以父子之親而傷至公之義，誠不曉聖朝所以然之意。

translations.literal: Yan again submitted a memorial saying: "Recently I ventured to plead for Jiangxia's pardon, not daring to let father-and-son affection injure the utmost public righteousness, yet truly not understanding why the holy court acts as it does.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted another memorial: "I have lately dared plead for clemency toward Jiangxia—not to let a father's love wound supreme public duty, but because I truly do not understand the court's intent.

sentences.zh: 若以狂主雖狂，而實是天子，江夏雖賢，實是人臣，先臣奉人臣逆人君為不可，未審今之嚴兵勁卒方指象魏者，其故何哉！

translations.literal: If one holds that though the mad ruler is mad he is in truth the Son of Heaven, and though Jiangxia is worthy he is in truth a subject, then my late father's serving as subject while opposing his ruler was impermissible—yet I do not see why stern troops and crack soldiers are now aimed at the Gate of Ivory; what is the reason!
translations.idiomatic: If a mad sovereign remains the Son of Heaven, and a worthy prince remains a subject, then my father's service as subject who opposed his ruler was wrong—yet why do elite troops now point at the imperial gate? For what cause!

sentences.zh: 臣所以不死，苟存視息，非有它故，所以待皇運之開泰，申忠魂之枉屈。

translations.literal: Your servant's reason for not dying and for lingering alive with breath drawn is no other: to await the opening of the imperial fortune and to plead the grievance of a loyal soul wronged.
translations.idiomatic: I have clung to life only to await the dawn of a new reign and to plead the wrong done a loyal ghost.

sentences.zh: 今皇運已開泰矣，而死社稷者返為賊臣，臣何用此生於陛下之世矣！

translations.literal: Now the imperial fortune has opened, yet he who died for the altars of state is instead made a traitorous minister—of what use is your servant's life in Your Majesty's age!
translations.idiomatic: That dawn has come—yet he who died for the state is branded a traitor. What use is my life in Your Majesty's world!

sentences.zh: 臣謹案鎮軍將軍臣穎冑、中領軍臣詳，皆社稷之也，同知先臣股肱江夏，匡濟王室，天命未遂，主亡與亡；

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that the Commander-in-Chief, your servant Ying Gou, and the Central Palace Guard Commander Xiang are both pillars of the state; they alike knew that my late father, arm and thigh of Jiangxia, sought to rescue the royal house; Heaven's mandate was not fulfilled, and when the lord perished they perished with him;
translations.idiomatic: I charge that the commander-in-chief Xiao Ying Gou and the central palace guard commander Xiao Xiang are pillars of the realm; both knew my father aided Jiangxia to save the dynasty, that Heaven's mandate failed, and that they died when their lord died;

sentences.zh: 而不為陛下瞥然一言。

translations.literal: yet they will not speak a single word for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: yet neither will speak one word to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 知而不言，不忠；

translations.literal: To know and not speak is disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: To know and remain silent is disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 不知而不言，不智也。

translations.literal: not to know and not speak is lack of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: not to know and remain silent is folly.

sentences.zh: 如以先臣遣使，江夏斬之；

translations.literal: If because my late father sent envoys, Jiangxia executed them;
translations.idiomatic: If Jiangxia killed envoys because my father sent them;

sentences.zh: ，則征東之驛使，何為見戮？

translations.literal: then why were the Eastern Expedition's courier envoys put to death?
translations.idiomatic: why were the Eastern Expedition's courier envoys slaughtered?

sentences.zh: 陛下斬征東之使，實詐山陽；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's execution of the Eastern Expedition's envoys was in truth deceit toward Shan Yang;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty slew the Eastern Expedition's envoys to deceive Shan Yang;

sentences.zh: 江夏違先臣之請，實謀孔矜。

translations.literal: Jiangxia's refusal of my late father's request was in truth plotting with Kong Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia's refusal of my father's plea was in truth plotting with Kong Jin.

sentences.zh: 天命有歸，故事業不遂耳。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate had its rightful bearer; that is why the enterprise did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate already had its owner; that is why the cause failed.

sentences.zh: 臣所言畢矣，乞就湯鑊！

translations.literal: Your servant's words are finished; I beg to enter the boiling cauldron!
translations.idiomatic: I have said all I can; I beg to be cast into the cauldron!

sentences.zh: 然臣雖萬沒，猶願陛下必申先臣。

translations.literal: Yet though your servant may die ten thousand deaths, I still hope Your Majesty will surely redress my late father.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though I die a thousand deaths, I still beg Your Majesty to vindicate my father.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 惻愴而申之，則天下伏；

translations.literal: If you redress him with compassion, the realm will submit;
translations.idiomatic: Redress him with compassion, and the realm will bow;

sentences.zh: 不則愴而申之，則天下叛。

translations.literal: if you redress him without compassion, the realm will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: redress him without true compassion, and the realm will rebel.

sentences.zh: 先臣之忠，有識所知，南、董之筆，千載可期，亦何待陛下屈申而為褒貶！

translations.literal: My late father's loyalty is known to the discerning; the pens of Nan and Dong may praise him for a thousand years—why wait for Your Majesty to bend and stretch in judgment!
translations.idiomatic: My father's loyalty is plain to the wise; historians like Nan Shi and Dong Hu will praise him for a thousand years—what need for Your Majesty to bend praise and blame to your will!

sentences.zh: 然小臣惓惓之愚，為陛下計耳。

translations.literal: Yet this petty official's earnest foolishness is offered only for Your Majesty's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this humble man's earnest folly is offered only for Your Majesty's sake.

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「其知卿惋切之懷，今當顯加贈謚。

translations.literal: " An edict replied: "We know your anguished heart; he shall now receive conspicuous posthumous honors and a title.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict answered: "We know your anguished heart; your father shall now receive conspicuous posthumous honors and a title.

sentences.zh: 」偃尋下獄死。

translations.literal: " Yan was soon cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan was soon thrown into prison and executed.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁卯，東昏侯以輔國將軍申冑監豫州事；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingmao, Marquis Donghun made the Assistant General Who Supports the State Shen Gou overseer of Yuzhou affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingmao, Marquis Donghun made Assistant General Who Supports the State Shen Gou overseer of Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 辛未，以光祿大夫張瑰鎮石頭。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he made the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Gui garrison Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he stationed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Gui at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 初，東昏侯遣陳伯之鎮江州，以為吳子陽等聲授。

translations.literal: Earlier, Marquis Donghun had sent Chen Bozhi to garrison Jiang Province as vocal support for Wu Ziyang and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Marquis Donghun had posted Chen Bozhi in Jiang Province to back Wu Ziyang and his allies.

sentences.zh: 子陽等既敗，蕭衍謂諸將曰：「用兵未必須實力，所聽威聲耳。

translations.literal: After Ziyang and the others were defeated, Xiao Yan said to the generals: "In war one need not always rely on real strength; what matters is the reputation one is heard to have.
translations.idiomatic: After Ziyang's defeat, Xiao Yan told his generals: "War does not always require brute force; what armies heed is renown.

sentences.zh: 今陳虎牙狠奔歸，尋陽人情理當恟懼，可傳檄而定也。

translations.literal: Now Chen Huya has fled home in panic; the people of Xunyang by rights ought to be terrified—this can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huya has fled home in disarray; Xunyang's people should be terrified already—we can take it with a proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 」乃命搜俘囚，得伯之幢主蘇隆之，厚加賜與，使說伯之，計即用為安東將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then ordered a search among prisoners and captives, found Bozhi's banner commander Su Longzhi, lavished gifts on him, and had him persuade Bozhi; the plan was at once to appoint him General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered prisoners searched, found Bozhi's banner commander Su Longzhi, rewarded him richly, and sent him to win Chen Bozhi over—promising him at once the post of general who pacifies the east and governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 伯之遣隆之返命，雖許歸附，而云「大軍未須遽下」。

translations.literal: Bozhi sent Longzhi back with his answer; though he promised submission, he said, "The great army need not hurry south.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi sent Longzhi back with his reply: he agreed to submit, yet said, "The main army need not march south in haste.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「伯之此言，意懷首鼠。

translations.literal: Yan said: "In these words Bozhi's mind harbors fence-sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Those words show Bozhi still sits on the fence.

sentences.zh: 及其猶豫，急往逼之，計無所出，勢不得不降。

translations.literal: While he still hesitates, press him hard; with no plan left, he will have no choice but to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While he wavers, press him hard; bereft of options, he will have no choice but to yield.

sentences.zh: 」乃命鄧元起引兵先下，楊公則徑掩柴桑，衍與諸將以次進路。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Deng Yuanqi to lead troops down first, Yang Gongze to strike straight at Chaisang, and Yan with the other generals to advance in turn along the route.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Deng Yuanqi to march down first, Yang Gongze to strike Chaisang directly, and himself with the other generals to follow in sequence.

sentences.zh: 元起將至尋陽，伯之收兵退保湖口，留陳虎牙守湓城。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi was about to reach Xunyang, Bozhi gathered his troops, withdrew to hold Hukou, and left Chen Huya to guard Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanqi neared Xunyang, Bozhi drew in his forces, fell back to defend Hukou, and left Chen Huya to hold Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 選曹郎吳興沈瑀說伯之迎衍。

translations.literal: Shen Yu of Wuxing, Gentleman of the Selection Bureau, urged Bozhi to welcome Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu of Wuxing, gentleman of the selection bureau, urged Bozhi to welcome Yan.

sentences.zh: 伯之泣曰：「余子在都，不能不愛。

translations.literal: Bozhi wept and said: "My sons are in the capital; I cannot but love them.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi wept: "My sons are in the capital—I cannot cease to love them.

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said: "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 人情匈匈，皆思改計；

translations.literal: Popular feeling is in turmoil; all are thinking to change their plans;
translations.idiomatic: The people's hearts are in turmoil; everyone is looking to change sides;

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，眾散難合。

translations.literal: if you do not act early, when the host disperses it will be hard to gather again.
translations.idiomatic: if you do not move soon, once the army scatters you cannot gather it again.

sentences.zh: 」丙子，衍至尋陽，伸之束甲請罪。

translations.literal: " On bingzi, Yan reached Xunyang; Shenzhi bound his armor and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: " On bingzi, Yan reached Xunyang; Chen Bozhi bound his armor in surrender and begged pardon.

sentences.zh: 初，新蔡太守席謙，父恭穆為鎮西司馬，為魚復侯子響所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi Qian, Administrator of Xincai—his father Gongmu had been Western Garrison Major and was killed by the Marquis of Yufu, Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi Qian, prefect of Xincai, had a father, Gongmu, who served as western garrison major and was killed by Marquis Yufu Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 謙從伯之鎮尋陽，聞衍東下，曰：「我家世忠貞，有殞不二。

translations.literal: Qian followed Bozhi to garrison Xunyang; hearing that Yan was marching east, he said: "My house has been loyal for generations; we die but once and do not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Qian had followed Bozhi to Xunyang. Hearing that Yan was marching east, he said: "My house has been loyal for generations—we die once and do not waver.

sentences.zh: 」伯之殺之。

translations.literal: " Bozhi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Bozhi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以伯之為江州刺史，虎牙為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On yimao, Bozhi was made Governor of Jiang Province and Huya Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Bozhi was made governor of Jiang Province and Huya governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 魯休烈、蕭瑰破劉孝慶等於峽口，任漾之戰死。

translations.literal: Lu Xiulie and Xiao Gui defeated Liu Xiaoqing and the rest at Xiakou; Ren Yangzhi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiulie and Xiao Gui routed Liu Xiaoqing and his forces at Xiakou; Ren Yangzhi fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 休烈等進至上明，江陵大震。

translations.literal: Xiulie and the others advanced to Shangming; Jiangling was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie and his allies pushed on to Shangming; Jiangling was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎冑恐，馳告蕭衍，令遣楊公則還援根本。

translations.literal: Xiao Ying Gou was afraid and urgently informed Xiao Yan, ordering him to send Yang Gongze back to rescue the root foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ying Gou, terrified, urgently asked Xiao Yan to send Yang Gongze back to defend their base.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「公則今溯流上江陵，雖至，何能及事！

translations.literal: Yan said: "If Gongze now goes upriver to Jiangling, even if he arrives, how can he affect the affair!
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied: "If Gongze turns upriver for Jiangling now, even should he arrive, what good will it do!

sentences.zh: 休烈等烏合之眾，尋自退散，政須少時持重耳。

translations.literal: Xiulie and the rest are a mob gathered in a flock; before long they will disperse of themselves—what is needed is only to hold firm a little while.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie's men are a rabble gathered in haste; they will soon scatter on their own—we need only hold steady awhile.

sentences.zh: 良須兵力，兩弟在雍，指遣往征，不為難至。

translations.literal: If troops are truly needed, my two younger brothers are in Yong; order them to march out and they will not be hard to reach.
translations.idiomatic: If we truly need force, my two brothers are in Yong; dispatch them and they can arrive without difficulty.

sentences.zh: 」穎冑乃遣軍主蔡道恭假節屯上明以拒蕭瑰。

translations.literal: " Ying Gou then sent the army commander Cai Daogong with provisional credentials to camp at Shangming and resist Xiao Gui.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying Gou then sent the army commander Cai Daogong with provisional credentials to camp at Shangming and block Xiao Gui.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，東昏侯以太子左率李居士總督西討諸軍事，頓新亭。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Marquis Donghun made the Crown Prince's Left Leader Li Jushi overall commander of the western punitive campaign and encamped at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Marquis Donghun made Crown Prince's Left Leader Li Jushi supreme commander of the western campaign and encamped at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙未，詔蕭衍若定京邑，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, an edict stated that if Xiao Yan pacified the capital region he might act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, an edict granted Xiao Yan discretionary authority should he pacify the capital.

sentences.zh: 衍留將軍鄭紹叔守尋陽，與陳伯之引兵東下，謂紹叔曰：「卿，吾之蕭何、寇恂也。

translations.literal: Yan left the general Zheng Shaoshu to guard Xunyang and marched east with Chen Bozhi, saying to Shaoshu: "You are my Xiao He and Kou Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan left General Zheng Shaoshu to hold Xunyang and marched east with Chen Bozhi, telling him: "You are my Xiao He and Kou Xun.

sentences.zh: 前塗不捷，我當其咎；

translations.literal: If the road ahead is not victorious, I shall bear the blame;
translations.idiomatic: If the advance fails, the fault is mine;

sentences.zh: 糧運不繼，卿任其責。

translations.literal: if grain transport does not continue, you shall bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: if the grain convoys falter, the fault is yours.

sentences.zh: 」紹叔流涕拜辭。

translations.literal: " Shaoshu wept as he bowed in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaoshu wept as he bowed farewell.

sentences.zh: 比克建康，紹叔督江、湘糧運，未嘗乏絕。

translations.literal: By the time Jiankang was taken, Shaoshu had overseen grain transport from Jiang and Xiang and it had never failed.
translations.idiomatic: By the fall of Jiankang, Shaoshu had overseen grain shipments from Jiang and Xiang without a single break in supply.

sentences.zh: 魏司州牧廣陽王嘉請築洛陽三百二十三坊，各方三百步，曰：「雖有暫勞，奸盜永息。

translations.literal: Jia, Prince of Guangyang and Governor of Si Province in Wei, requested the building of three hundred twenty-three wards in Luoyang, each three hundred paces square, saying: "Though there is temporary labor, thieves and robbers will forever cease.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Prince Guangyang Jia, governor of Si Province, proposed building three hundred twenty-three wards in Luoyang, each three hundred paces square, saying: "Though the labor is brief, banditry will cease for good.

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，詔發畿內夫五萬人築之，四旬而罷。

translations.literal: " On dingyou, an edict ordered five hundred thousand laborers from the inner commanderies to build them; in forty days the work was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " On dingyou an edict drafted five hundred thousand laborers from the metropolitan region; in forty days the work ended.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏立皇后于氏。

translations.literal: On jihai, Wei established the Empress née Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Northern Wei installed Empress Yu.

sentences.zh: 後，征虜將軍勁之女；

translations.literal: The empress was daughter of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians Jin;
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of General Who Conquers the Barbarians Jin;

sentences.zh: 勁，烈之弟也。

translations.literal: Jin was the younger brother of Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was the younger brother of Lie.

sentences.zh: 自祖父栗磾以來，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From their grandfather Li Di onward, the family had been noble and flourishing for generations: one empress, four posthumous dukes, three commanders-in-chief, two chiefs of the Masters of Writing, and three founding marquises.
translations.idiomatic: From their grandfather Li Di onward the clan had risen for generations: one empress, four men posthumously made dukes, three commanders-in-chief, two chiefs of the masters of writing, and three founding marquises.

sentences.zh: 甲申，東昏侯以李居士為江州刺史，冠軍將軍王珍國為雍州刺史，建安王寶寅為荊州刺史，輔國將軍申冑監郢州，龍驤將軍扶風馬仙玭監豫州，驍騎將軍徐元稱監徐州軍事。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Marquis Donghun made Li Jushi Governor of Jiang Province, the Champion General Wang Zhenguo Governor of Yong Province, the Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin Governor of Jing Province, the Assistant General Who Supports the State Shen Gou overseer of Ying Province, the Dragon-Prancing General Ma Xianbi of Fufeng overseer of Yuzhou, and the Valiant Cavalry General Xu Yuancheng overseer of military affairs in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Marquis Donghun appointed Li Jushi governor of Jiang Province, Champion General Wang Zhenguo governor of Yong Province, Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin governor of Jing Province, Assistant General Who Supports the State Shen Gou overseer of Ying Province, Dragon-Prancing General Ma Xianbi of Fufeng overseer of Yuzhou, and Valiant Cavalry General Xu Yuancheng overseer of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 珍國，廣之之子也。

translations.literal: Zhenguo was the son of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo was Guang's son.

sentences.zh: 是日，蕭衍前軍至蕪湖；

translations.literal: That same day, Xiao Yan's vanguard reached Wuhu;
translations.idiomatic: That day Xiao Yan's vanguard reached Wuhu;

sentences.zh: 申冑軍二萬人棄姑孰走，衍進軍，據之。

translations.literal: Shen Gou's army of twenty thousand abandoned Guzhu and fled; Yan advanced and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Gou's twenty thousand men abandoned Guzhu and fled; Yan pressed forward and occupied it.

sentences.zh: 戊申，東昏侯以後軍參軍蕭瑰為司州刺史，前輔國將軍魯休烈為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On wushen, Marquis Donghun made the Rear Army Staff Officer Xiao Gui Governor of Si Province and the former Assistant General Who Supports the State Lu Xiulie Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Marquis Donghun made Rear Army staff officer Xiao Gui governor of Si Province and former Assistant General Who Supports the State Lu Xiulie governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍之克江、郢也，東昏侯游騁如舊，謂茹法珍曰：「須來至白門前，當一決。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan had taken Jiang and Ying, Marquis Donghun roved and hunted as before, saying to Ru Fazhen: "When they come to before the White Gate, we shall settle it in one fight.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Yan captured Jiang and Ying, Marquis Donghun still roved and hunted as before. He told Ru Fazhen, "When they reach the White Gate, we shall settle it in one battle.

sentences.zh: 」衍至近道，乃聚兵為固守之計，簡二尚方、二冶囚徒以配軍；

translations.literal: " When Yan drew near, Donghun then gathered troops for a plan of stubborn defense, selecting convicts from the two Palace Workshops and two Smelteries to assign to the army;
translations.idiomatic: " As Yan drew near, he massed troops for a last-ditch defense, drafting convicts from the two palace workshops and two smelteries into the ranks;

sentences.zh: 其不可活者，於朱雀門內日斬百餘人。

translations.literal: those who could not be kept alive he had beheaded by the hundred each day within the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: those deemed beyond saving he had beheaded by the hundred each day inside the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 衍遣曹景宗等進頓江寧。

translations.literal: Yan sent Cao Jingzong and others to advance and encamp at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Cao Jingzong and others forward to encamp at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，李居士自新亭選精騎一千至江寧。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Li Jushi selected a thousand crack horsemen from Xinting and came to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Li Jushi led a thousand picked horsemen from Xinting to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 景宗始至，營壘未立，且師行日久，器甲穿弊。

translations.literal: Jingzong had just arrived; his camps and ramparts were not yet set, and the army had marched long; weapons and armor were worn through.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong had only just arrived; his camp was not yet built, and after a long march his men's arms and armor were worn out.

sentences.zh: 居士望而輕之，鼓噪直前薄之；

translations.literal: Jushi saw this and held them light; drumming and shouting, he pressed straight forward to close with them;
translations.idiomatic: Jushi looked on and despised them; drumming and shouting, he charged straight at their line;

sentences.zh: 景宗奮擊，破之，因乘勝而前，逕至皁莢橋。

translations.literal: Jingzong struck back with spirit, routed them, and riding victory pressed on straight to Zaojia Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong struck back hard, broke them, and pressing his advantage marched straight to Zaojia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 於是王茂、鄧元超、呂僧珍進據赤鼻邏，新亭城主江道林引兵出戰，眾軍擒之於陳。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Mao, Deng Yuanchao, and Lü Sengzhen advanced and seized Chibei Market; Jiang Daolin, commandant of Xinting, led troops out to fight, and the host captured him in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, Deng Yuanchao, and Lü Sengzhen then seized Chibei Market. Jiang Daolin, lord of Xinting, led his men out to fight and was taken in the field.

sentences.zh: 衍至新林，命王茂進據越城，鄧元起據道士墩，陳伯之據籬門，呂僧珍據白板橋。

translations.literal: Yan reached Xinlin and ordered Wang Mao to advance and hold Yue City, Deng Yuanqi to hold Daoshi Mound, Chen Bozhi to hold Fence Gate, and Lü Sengzhen to hold Whiteboard Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached Xinlin and ordered Wang Mao to hold Yue City, Deng Yuanqi Daoshi Mound, Chen Bozhi Fence Gate, and Lü Sengzhen Whiteboard Bridge.

sentences.zh: 李居士覘之僧珍眾少，帥銳卒萬人直來薄壘。

translations.literal: Li Jushi reconnoitered and saw Sengzhen's force was few; he led ten thousand crack soldiers straight to press their ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jushi saw that Sengzhen had few men and led ten thousand elite troops straight at his camp.

sentences.zh: 僧珍曰：「吾眾少，不可逆戰，可勿遙射，須至塹裡，當並力破之。

translations.literal: Sengzhen said: "Our force is few; we cannot meet them in battle. Do not shoot from afar; wait until they reach the ditch, then we shall combine strength and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen said, "We are too few to meet them head-on. Hold your fire from afar; when they reach the ditch we shall strike together and break them.

sentences.zh: 」俄而皆越塹拔柵。

translations.literal: " In a moment all had crossed the ditch and torn up the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: " In a moment they had all crossed the ditch and torn down the palisade.

sentences.zh: 僧珍分人上城，矢石俱發，自帥馬步三百人出其後，城上人復逾城而下，內外奮擊，居士敗走，獲取器甲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Sengzhen divided men to mount the wall; arrows and stones flew together; he himself led three hundred horse and foot out behind them; men atop the wall again leaped down from the wall; inside and outside they struck with spirit; Jushi was defeated and fled, and arms and armor captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen sent men up the wall with a storm of arrows and stones, himself led three hundred horse and foot around their rear, and his men on the wall leaped down to join the fight. Attacked from within and without, Jushi was routed. The arms and armor taken were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 居士請於東昏侯，燒南岸邑屋以開戰場，自大航以西、新亭以北皆盡。

translations.literal: Jushi requested of Marquis Donghun that the towns and houses on the south bank be burned to clear a battlefield; from the Great Ferry west and Xinting north all were consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi asked Marquis Donghun to burn the towns and houses on the south bank to clear a battlefield; from the Great Ferry west to Xinting north nothing was left standing.

sentences.zh: 衍諸弟皆自建康自拔赴軍。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brothers all escaped from Jiankang on their own and joined the army.
translations.idiomatic: All of Yan's younger brothers slipped out of Jiankang on their own and joined his army.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，東昏侯遣征虜將軍王珍國、軍主胡虎牙將精兵十萬餘人陳於朱雀航南，宦官王寶孫持白虎幡督戰，開航背水，以絕歸路。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Marquis Donghun sent Campaigning General Wang Zhenguo and Army Commander Hu Huya to lead more than a hundred thousand crack troops and array them south of the Vermilion Bird Ford; the eunuch Wang Baosun held the White Tiger banner to oversee battle; they opened the ford with water at their backs to cut off the road of return.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Marquis Donghun sent Campaigning General Wang Zhenguo and army commander Hu Huya with more than a hundred thousand elite troops to form battle lines south of the Vermilion Bird Ford. The eunuch Wang Baosun bore the White Tiger banner to direct the fight. They opened the ford and faced the water behind them to cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 衍軍小卻，王茂下馬，單刀直前，其甥韋欣慶執鐵纏槊以翼之，衝擊東軍，應時而陷。

translations.literal: Yan's army drew back slightly; Wang Mao dismounted, took a single blade, and pressed straight forward; his nephew Wei Xinqing wielded an iron-shod lance to flank him; they charged the eastern army and broke it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's army gave ground slightly. Wang Mao dismounted, drew a single blade, and charged straight ahead; his nephew Wei Xinqing flanked him with an iron-shod lance. They smashed the eastern army on the spot.

sentences.zh: 曹景宗縱兵乘之，呂僧珍縱火焚其營，將士皆殊死戰，鼓噪震天地。

translations.literal: Cao Jingzong loosed his troops to ride the advantage; Lü Sengzhen set fire and burned their camp; officers and soldiers all fought to the death; drums and shouts shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong drove his men in pursuit; Lü Sengzhen set fire to their camp. Officers and soldiers fought as if unto death; drums and shouts shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 珍國等眾軍不能抗，王寶孫切罵諸將帥，直閣將軍席豪發憤突陳而死。

translations.literal: Zhenguo and the host of armies could not resist; Wang Baosun bitterly cursed the generals; the Direct Gate General Xi Hao, in a burst of rage, charged the line and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo's armies could not hold. Wang Baosun cursed the generals bitterly. Direct Gate General Xi Hao, in a fury, charged the line and was killed.

sentences.zh: 豪，驍將也，既死，士卒土崩，赴淮死者無數，積屍與航等，後至者乘以之以濟。

translations.literal: Hao was a fierce general; once he died, the soldiers collapsed like earth; those who rushed into the Huai to die were beyond count; corpses piled level with the ford, and those who came later crossed on them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was a fierce fighter; once he fell, the army collapsed. Countless men drowned in the Huai; corpses piled level with the ford, and those who came after crossed on the dead.

sentences.zh: 於是東昏侯諸軍望之皆潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon all Marquis Donghun's armies, seeing this, routed.
translations.idiomatic: At that sight all of Marquis Donghun's armies broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 衍軍長驅至宣陽門，諸將移稍前。

translations.literal: Yan's army drove at full speed to the Xuanyang Gate; the generals shifted their positions slightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's army swept on to the Xuanyang Gate as the generals edged their lines forward.

sentences.zh: 陳伯之屯西明門，每城中有降人出，伯之輒呼與耳語。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi was encamped at the Ximing Gate; whenever someone from the city came out to surrender, Bozhi would call him and speak in his ear.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi held the Ximing Gate. Whenever a defector came out of the city, Bozhi would call him aside and whisper in his ear.

sentences.zh: 衍恐其復懷翻覆，密語伯之曰：「聞城中甚忿卿舉江州降，欲遣刺客中卿，宜以為慮」。

translations.literal: Yan feared he might again harbor thoughts of turning; he spoke secretly to Bozhi: "I hear the city is greatly angry that you raised Jiang Province in surrender and wishes to send assassins against you—you should take this to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yan feared he might waver again and told him privately, "I hear the city is furious that you surrendered Jiang Province and means to send assassins against you. You should beware."

sentences.zh: 伯之未之信。

translations.literal: Bozhi did not yet believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi did not yet believe him.

sentences.zh: 會東昏侯將鄭伯倫來降，衍使伯倫過伯之，謂曰：「城中甚忿卿，欲遣信誘卿以封賞，須卿復降，當生割卿手足；

translations.literal: It happened that Donghun's general Zheng Bolun came to surrender; Yan had Bolun pass by Bozhi and say: "The city is greatly angry with you and wishes to send envoys to lure you with titles and rewards; if you should surrender again, they will cut off your hands and feet while you live;
translations.idiomatic: Just then Marquis Donghun's officer Zheng Bolun came over to Yan. Yan sent Bolun to Bozhi with this message: "The city is furious with you. They mean to lure you back with titles and rewards; if you surrender again they will cut off your hands and feet while you live;

sentences.zh: 卿若不降，復欲遣刺客殺卿。

translations.literal: if you do not surrender, they again wish to send assassins to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: if you do not yield, they will send assassins to kill you.

sentences.zh: 宜深為備。

translations.literal: You should guard deeply against this.
translations.idiomatic: Guard yourself well.

sentences.zh: 」伯之懼，自是始無異志。

translations.literal: " Bozhi was afraid; from then on he had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Bozhi was terrified and from then on held no other allegiance.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，東昏寧朔將軍徐元瑜以東府城降。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Marquis Donghun's General Who Pacifies the North Xu Yuancheng surrendered the Eastern Mansion city.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Marquis Donghun's General Who Pacifies the North Xu Yuancheng surrendered the Eastern Mansion.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史桓和入援，屯東宮。

translations.literal: Huan He, Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces, entered to reinforce and encamped at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, governor of Qing and Ji provinces, marched in to reinforce and encamped at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 己卯，和許東昏，雲出戰，因以其眾來降。

translations.literal: On jimao, He promised Donghun he would go out to fight, then brought his host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, He promised Donghun he would go out to fight, then brought his entire force over to Yan.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫張瑰棄石頭還宮。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Gui abandoned Stone City and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Gui abandoned Stone City and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 李居士以新亭降於衍，琅邪城主張木亦降。

translations.literal: Li Jushi surrendered Xinting to Yan; Zhang Mu, lord of Langye, also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jushi surrendered Xinting to Yan, and Zhang Mu, lord of Langye, surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衍鎮石頭，命諸軍攻六門。

translations.literal: On renwu, Yan garrisoned Stone City and ordered the armies to attack the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Yan took Stone City and ordered his armies to assault the six gates.

sentences.zh: 東昏燒門內營署、官府，驅逼士民，悉入宮城，閉門自守。

translations.literal: Donghun burned the camps, offices, and government halls inside the gates, drove and pressed scholars and commoners, all into the palace city, shut the gates, and held himself within.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun burned the camps and government offices inside the gates, drove scholars and commoners into the palace city, shut the gates, and held himself within.

sentences.zh: 衍命諸軍築長圍守之。

translations.literal: Yan ordered the armies to build a long encirclement and besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered his armies to build a long encirclement and lay siege.

sentences.zh: 楊公則屯領軍府壘北樓，與南掖門相對，嘗登樓望戰。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze was encamped at the north tower of the Army Director's fortress rampart, facing the Southern Flank Gate; he once mounted the tower to watch the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze held the north tower of the Army Director's fortress, facing the Southern Flank Gate, and once climbed the tower to watch the battle.

sentences.zh: 城中遙見麾蓋，以神鋒弩射之，矢貫胡床，左右失色。

translations.literal: Men in the city saw his banner and canopy from afar and shot at him with divine-edge crossbows; an arrow pierced his folding camp-chair; those at his side turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Men in the city saw his banner and canopy from afar and shot at him with divine-edge crossbows. An arrow pierced his camp chair; his attendants turned pale.

sentences.zh: 公則曰：「幾中吾腳！

translations.literal: Gongze said: "It nearly hit my foot!
translations.idiomatic: Gongze said, "That nearly took my foot!

sentences.zh: 」談笑如初。

translations.literal: " He talked and laughed as at first.
translations.idiomatic: " He talked and laughed as before.

sentences.zh: 東昏夜選勇士攻公則柵，軍中驚擾；

translations.literal: Donghun by night selected brave warriors to attack Gongze's palisade; the army was alarmed and thrown into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Donghun by night sent picked warriors to assault Gongze's palisade, throwing his camp into alarm;

sentences.zh: 公則堅臥不起，徐命擊之，東昏兵乃退。

translations.literal: Gongze lay firm and did not rise, slowly ordered a strike, and Donghun's troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze lay still and did not rise, then calmly ordered a counterattack; Donghun's men withdrew.

sentences.zh: 公則所領皆湘州人，素號怯懦，城中輕之，每出蕩，輒先犯公則壘；

translations.literal: Those Gongze led were all men of Xiang Province, long known as timid and weak; the city held them light; whenever they sallied forth, they always first attacked Gongze's rampart;
translations.idiomatic: Gongze's men were all from Xiang Province, long reputed cowards; the city despised them and whenever they sallied always struck Gongze's camp first;

sentences.zh: 公則獎厲軍士，克獲更多。

translations.literal: Gongze encouraged and urged his soldiers, and captures and gains were the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze exhorted his men, and their captures and victories grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 先是，東昏遣軍主左僧慶屯京口，常僧景屯廣陵，李叔獻屯瓜步；

translations.literal: Earlier, Donghun had sent Army Commander Zuo Sengqing to encamp at Jingkou, Chang Sengjing at Guangling, and Li Shuxian at Guabu;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Donghun had posted army commander Zuo Sengqing at Jingkou, Chang Sengjing at Guangling, and Li Shuxian at Guabu;

sentences.zh: 及申冑自姑孰奔歸，使屯破墩，以為東北聲援。

translations.literal: when Shen Gou fled back from Guzhu, he had them encamp at Podun as a northeastern voice of support.
translations.idiomatic: when Shen Gou fled from Guzhu, Donghun posted them at Podun to support the northeast.

sentences.zh: 至是，衍遣使曉諭，皆帥其眾來降。

translations.literal: At this time Yan sent envoys to enlighten and instruct them; all led their hosts to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yan sent envoys to win them over, and all led their forces to surrender.

sentences.zh: 衍遣弟輔國將軍秀鎮京口，輔國將軍恢鎮破墩，從弟寧朔將軍景鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Yan sent his younger brother the Assistant General Who Supports the State Xiu to garrison Jingkou, the Assistant General Who Supports the State Hui to garrison Podun, and his cousin the General Who Pacifies the North Jing to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yan posted his brother Assistant General Who Supports the State Xiu at Jingkou, another brother Hui at Podun, and his cousin General Who Pacifies the North Jing at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙申，魏以驃騎大將軍穆亮為司空；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingshen, Wei made the Swift Cavalry General Mu Liang Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen, Northern Wei made Swift Cavalry General Mu Liang minister of works;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以北海王詳為太傅，領司徒，初，詳欲奪彭城王勰司徒，故譖而黜之；

translations.literal: on dingyou, made the Prince of Beihai Xiang Grand Tutor and concurrent Minister of Education; earlier Xiang had wished to seize the Prince of Pengcheng Xie's post as Minister of Education, and therefore slandered and removed him;
translations.idiomatic: on dingyou appointed Prince of Beihai Xiang grand tutor and concurrent minister of education. Earlier Xiang had wanted Xie's post as minister of education and had slandered him into dismissal;

sentences.zh: 既而畏人議己，故但為大將軍，至是乃居之。

translations.literal: afterward he feared men's criticism of himself and therefore took only the post of Grand General; only now did he occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: then, fearing criticism, he had taken only the post of grand general; only now did he assume the ministry.

sentences.zh: 詳貴盛翕赫，將作大匠王遇多隨詳所欲，私以官物給之。

translations.literal: Xiang was noble, flourishing, and blazing in glory; the Master of Works Wang Yu often followed whatever Xiang wished and privately gave him government goods.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's glory blazed; Master of Works Wang Yu often indulged his wishes and privately gave him government goods.

sentences.zh: 司空長史於忠責遇於詳前曰：「殿下，國之周公，阿衡王室，所須材用，自應關旨；

translations.literal: The Minister of Works' chief clerk Yu Zhong reproached Yu before Xiang, saying: "Your Highness is the Duke of Zhou of the state, who balances and assists the royal house; whatever materials are needed should naturally pass through imperial approval;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works chief clerk Yu Zhong rebuked Wang Yu before Xiang: "Your Highness is the state's Duke of Zhou, who steadies the throne. Whatever materials you need should pass through proper channels;

sentences.zh: 何至阿諛附勢，損公惠私也！

translations.literal: how could it reach to fawning and clinging to power, harming the public and favoring the private!
translations.idiomatic: how could you sink to fawning on power, harming the public purse for private gain!

sentences.zh: 」遇既踧□，詳亦慚謝。

translations.literal: " Yu had already flinched; Xiang also apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yu shrank back abashed; Xiang apologized as well.

sentences.zh: 忠每以鯁直為詳所忿，嘗罵忠曰：「我憂在前見爾死，不憂爾見我死時也！

translations.literal: Zhong's blunt uprightness was often an object of Xiang's resentment; he once cursed Zhong: "I worry that I shall see you die first, not that you shall see the time of my death!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang often resented Zhong's blunt honesty and once cursed him: "I worry I shall see you die first, not that you will see me die!

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「人生於世，自有定分；

translations.literal: " Zhong said: "Life in the world has its own allotted portion;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong said, "Life has its allotted span;

sentences.zh: 若應死於王手，避亦不免；

translations.literal: if one ought to die by the prince's hand, even fleeing one cannot escape;
translations.idiomatic: if I am fated to die by your hand, flight will not save me;

sentences.zh: 若其不爾，王不能殺！

translations.literal: if it is not so, the prince cannot kill!
translations.idiomatic: if not, you cannot kill me!

sentences.zh: 」忠以討咸陽王禧功，封魏郡公，遷散騎常侍，兼武衛將軍。

translations.literal: " For Zhong's merit in punishing the Prince of Xianyang Xi, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery, promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and concurrently made Military Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: " For his merit in punishing Prince of Xianyang Xi, Zhong was enfeoffed as duke of Wei commandery, promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and made military guard general as well.

sentences.zh: 詳因忠表讓之際，密勸魏主以忠為列卿，令解左右，聽其上爵，於是詔停其封，優進太府卿。

translations.literal: Xiang, taking advantage of Zhong's memorial of refusal, secretly urged the Wei ruler to make Zhong a ranked minister, have him released from attendance at the ruler's side, and allow him to ascend in rank; thereupon an edict halted his enfeoffment and advanced him in favor to Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, exploiting Zhong's memorial declining honors, secretly urged the Wei emperor to make Zhong a ranked minister, remove him from the ruler's side, and let him rise in rank. An edict then halted his enfeoffment and promoted him to grand steward instead.

sentences.zh: 巴東獻武公蕭穎冑以蕭瑰與蔡道恭相持不決，憂憤成疾；

translations.literal: Xiao Ying Gou, Duke of Wuxian of Badong, because Xiao Gui and Cai Daogong were locked in stalemate without decision, worried and raged into illness;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ying Gou, Duke Wuxian of Badong, fell ill with worry because Xiao Gui and Cai Daogong remained locked in stalemate;

sentences.zh: 壬午，卒。

translations.literal: On renwu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he died.

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳秘之，使似其書者假為教命，密報蕭衍，衍亦秘之。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang kept it secret, had one whose hand resembled his forge orders in his name, secretly reported to Xiao Yan, and Yan also kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang kept the death secret, had someone forge orders in Ying Gou's hand, and secretly informed Xiao Yan, who also concealed it.

sentences.zh: 詳徵兵雍州，蕭偉遣蕭心詹將兵赴之。

translations.literal: Xiang raised troops in Yong Province; Xiao Wei sent Xiao Xinzhan to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang raised troops in Yong Province; Xiao Wei sent Xiao Xinzhan with an army to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 瑰等聞建康已危，眾懼而潰，瑰及魯休烈皆降。

translations.literal: Gui and the rest heard Jiankang was already in peril; the host feared and collapsed; Gui and Lu Xiulie both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and his allies heard Jiankang was in peril; their armies panicked and broke. Gui and Lu Xiulie both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乃發穎冑喪，贈侍中、丞相；

translations.literal: Only then was Ying Gou's funeral proclaimed; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was Ying Gou's death announced; he was posthumously honored as palace attendant and chancellor;

sentences.zh: 於是眾望盡歸於衍。

translations.literal: thereupon the hopes of all turned wholly to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and all hopes turned to Yan.

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳請與蕭憺共參軍國，詔以詳為侍中、尚書右僕射，尋除使持節、撫軍將軍荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang requested to join Xiao Dan in administering state and army affairs; an edict made Xiang Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and soon removed him to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang asked to administer state affairs jointly with Xiao Dan. An edict made Xiang palace attendant and right vice director of the masters of writing, then envoy bearing staff of authority, general who pacifies the army, and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 詳固讓於憺，乃以憺行荊州府州事。

translations.literal: Xiang firmly yielded to Dan; thereupon Dan was made to act in Jing prefectural and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang firmly yielded to Dan, who was then put in charge of Jing prefectural and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏改築圜丘於伊水之陽；

translations.literal: Wei rebuilt the Round Mound Altar on the south bank of the Yi River;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei rebuilt the Round Mound Altar on the south bank of the Yi River;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，始祀於其上。

translations.literal: on yimao, they first sacrificed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao they first sacrificed there.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮南將軍元英上書曰：「蕭寶卷驕縱日甚，虐害無辜。

translations.literal: Wei's General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying submitted a memorial saying: "Xiao Baojuan grows daily more arrogant and unrestrained, cruelly harming the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying submitted a memorial: "Xiao Baojuan grows more arrogant and cruel by the day, slaughtering the innocent.

sentences.zh: 其雍州刺史蕭衍東伐秣陵，掃土興兵，順流而下；

translations.literal: His Governor of Yong Province Xiao Yan campaigns east against Moling, sweeps the land and raises troops, and comes down with the current;
translations.idiomatic: His governor of Yong Province, Xiao Yan, marches east against Moling, raises armies across the land, and comes downriver;

sentences.zh: 唯有孤城，更無重衛，乃皇天授我之日，曠載一逢之秋；

translations.literal: there is only a lone city and no further heavy guard—this is the day Heaven grants us, an autumn met once in vast ages;
translations.idiomatic: only a lone city remains, with no strong guard—this is the day Heaven grants us, an opportunity that comes once in ages;

sentences.zh: 此而不乘，將欲何待！

translations.literal: if we do not ride this, what shall we wait for!
translations.idiomatic: if we do not seize it now, what are we waiting for!

sentences.zh: 臣乞躬帥步騎三萬，直指沔陰，據襄陽之城，斷黑水之路。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to lead in person thirty thousand foot and horse, strike straight at the Mian's north bank, hold the city of Xiangyang, and cut the road of the Black Water.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to lead thirty thousand foot and horse in person straight to the north bank of the Mian, hold Xiangyang, and cut the Black Water route.

sentences.zh: 昏虐君臣，自相魚肉；

translations.literal: The benighted and cruel ruler and his ministers devour one another like fish and flesh;
translations.idiomatic: The benighted ruler and his ministers tear one another apart;

sentences.zh: 我居上流，威震遐邇，長驅南出，進拔江陵，則三楚之地一朝可收，岷、蜀之道自成斷絕。

translations.literal: we hold the upper stream, our might shakes far and near; driving long south, advancing to take Jiangling, then the land of the Three Chu can in one morning be gathered, and the roads of Min and Shu will of themselves be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: holding the upper river, our might will shake the realm; driving south to take Jiangling, we can seize the Three Chu in a morning and cut off the roads to Min and Shu.

sentences.zh: 又命揚、徐二州聲言俱舉，建業窮蹙，魚游釜中，可以齊文軌而大同，混天地而為一。

translations.literal: Further order Yang and Xu Provinces to proclaim together that all rise; Jianye is cornered and straitened, a fish swimming in a cauldron—we can align the written and the track and achieve great unity, blend heaven and earth into one.
translations.idiomatic: Order Yang and Xu to rise together in name; Jianye is trapped like a fish in a cauldron—we can unite the realm, align all under one rule, and merge heaven and earth into one.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下獨決聖心，無取疑議；

translations.literal: Your servant bows that Your Majesty alone decide with sage heart and take no doubtful counsel;
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide alone with a sage heart and heed no doubters;

sentences.zh: 此期脫爽，併吞無日。

translations.literal: if this term passes in vain, there will be no day for swallowing whole.
translations.idiomatic: if this moment slips away, conquest may never come again.

sentences.zh: 」事寢不報。

translations.literal: " The matter was shelved; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 車騎大將軍源懷上言：「蕭衍內侮，寶卷孤危，廣陵、淮陰等戍皆觀望得失。

translations.literal: Chariots and Cavalry General Yuan Huai submitted: "Xiao Yan insults within; Baojuan is lone and perilous; the garrisons at Guangling, Huaiyin, and the like all watch to see which side gains or loses.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and Cavalry General Yuan Huai submitted: "Xiao Yan attacks within; Baojuan stands alone and endangered; garrisons at Guangling, Huaiyin, and elsewhere all watch which way fortune turns.

sentences.zh: 斯實天啟上期，併吞之會；

translations.literal: This is truly Heaven's opening of a supreme term, the meeting for swallowing whole;
translations.idiomatic: This is truly Heaven opening the supreme moment for conquest;

sentences.zh: 宜東西齊舉，以成席捲之勢。

translations.literal: east and west should rise together to complete a rolling-up momentum.
translations.idiomatic: east and west should strike together to complete a sweeping advance.

sentences.zh: 若使蕭衍克濟，上下同心，豈惟後圖之難，亦恐揚州危逼。

translations.literal: If Xiao Yan succeeds in his enterprise and above and below share one heart, not only will later designs be hard, but I fear Yang Province will be pressed in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiao Yan succeeds and court and army unite, not only will later conquest grow hard—we may find Yang Province itself in peril.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 壽春之去建康才七百里，山川水陸，皆彼所諳。

translations.literal: Shouchun is only seven hundred li from Jiankang; mountains, rivers, water, and land—all are terrain they know well.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun lies only seven hundred li from Jiankang; every mountain, river, and route is terrain they know intimately.

sentences.zh: 彼若內外無虞，君臣分定，乘舟藉水，倏忽而至，未易當也。

translations.literal: If they have no worry within or without, ruler and minister roles fixed, riding boats and borrowing water, they arrive in a flash—not easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: If they are secure within and without, sovereign and ministers settled, they can come by boat in a flash—hard to withstand.

sentences.zh: 今寶卷都邑有土崩之憂，邊城無繼授之望，廓清江表，正在今日。

translations.literal: Now Baojuan's capital has the worry of earth collapsing; border cities have no hope of continued relief; to clear and pacify the lands south of the Yang is just in this day.
translations.idiomatic: Now Baojuan's capital totters; border cities expect no relief; to clear the lands south of the Yang must be done today.

sentences.zh: 」魏主乃以任城王澄為都督淮南諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，使為經略；

translations.literal: " The Wei ruler then made the Prince of Rencheng Cheng Grand Marshal over all military affairs in Huainan, General Who Guards the South, Opener of the Office with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yang Province, and had him conduct strategy;
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei emperor then made Prince of Rencheng Cheng grand marshal over Huainan, general who guards the south, opener of an office equal to the three excellencies, and governor of Yang Province to direct strategy;

sentences.zh: 既而不果。

translations.literal: but in the end it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: but in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 懷，賀之子也。

translations.literal: Huai was the son of He.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was He's son.

sentences.zh: 東豫州刺史田益宗上表曰：「蕭氏亂常，君臣交爭，江外州鎮，中分為兩，東西抗峙，已淹歲時。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong, Governor of Eastern Yu Province, submitted a memorial saying: "The Xiao house has disturbed the constant order; ruler and ministers contend; prefectures and garrisons beyond the Yang are split in two; east and west stand opposed—already years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yu governor Tian Yizong submitted a memorial: "The Xiao house has thrown the realm into chaos; ruler and ministers fight one another; commanderies south of the Yang are split in two and have faced off for years.

sentences.zh: 民庶窮於轉輸，甲兵疲於戰鬥，事救於目前，力盡於麾下，無暇外維州鎮，綱紀庶方，籓城棋立，孤存而已。

translations.literal: The people are exhausted by transport and relay; armor and troops are worn out by battle; affairs are saved only before the eyes; strength is spent under the commander's banner; there is no leisure to maintain outer prefectures and garrisons or order the distant regions; frontier cities stand like chess pieces, surviving alone—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The people are exhausted by transport; armies are worn out by battle. Each side tends only what lies before it; strength is spent under its own banners. Neither can spare force to hold distant commanderies; frontier cities stand like chess pieces, barely surviving alone.

sentences.zh: 不乘機電掃，廓彼蠻疆，恐後之經略，未易於此。

translations.literal: If we do not seize the moment and sweep like lightning to clear that barbarian frontier, I fear later strategy will not be easier than this.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not seize the moment and sweep their southern frontier clean, later campaigns may never be easier than this.

sentences.zh: 且故壽春雖平，三面仍梗，鎮守之宜，實須豫設。

translations.literal: Moreover, though old Shouchun is pacified, on three sides it is still blocked; what is fitting for garrison and defense truly must be set in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though old Shouchun is pacified, three sides remain blocked; garrisons must be planned in advance.

sentences.zh: 義陽差近淮源，利涉津要，朝廷行師，必由此道。

translations.literal: Yiyang is rather near the Huai's source, advantageous for crossing strategic fords; when the court dispatches troops, it must go by this route.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang lies close to the headwaters of the Huai and commands the key river crossings; any army the court sends south must pass that way.

sentences.zh: 若江南一平，有事淮外，須乘夏水汎長，列舟長淮；

translations.literal: If the lands south of the Yangtze are pacified at a stroke and affairs arise beyond the Huai, one must take advantage of the summer flood when the waters swell and array vessels along the Long Huai;
translations.idiomatic: When the south is subdued in one sweep and campaigns open beyond the Huai, we must ride the summer rise and mass a fleet on the Long Huai,

sentences.zh: 師赴壽春，須從義陽之北，便是居我喉要，在慮彌深。

translations.literal: Troops hurrying to Shouchun must pass north of Yiyang—that would place them at our throat, and the concern runs all the deeper.
translations.idiomatic: and any force bound for Shouchun must come north of Yiyang—right at our throat. The worry could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 義陽之滅，今實時矣。

translations.literal: The destruction of Yiyang—now is truly the time.
translations.idiomatic: The time to destroy Yiyang is now.

sentences.zh: 度彼不過須精卒一萬二千；

translations.literal: Estimating the enemy, they would need no more than twelve thousand picked troops;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, I judge, would require no more than twelve thousand elite soldiers;

sentences.zh: 然行師之法，貴張形勢。

translations.literal: Yet in the art of campaigning, what is prized is projecting overwhelming force.
translations.idiomatic: but the art of war prizes the display of overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 請使兩荊之眾西擬隨、雍，揚州之卒頓於建安，得捍三關之援；

translations.literal: I request that the armies of the two Jing provinces feint west toward Sui and Yong, while Yangzhou's soldiers encamp at Jian'an to secure support for the Three Passes;
translations.idiomatic: Send the two Jing armies west in a feint toward Sui and Yong, station Yangzhou's troops at Jian'an to shield the Three Passes,

sentences.zh: 然後二豫之軍直據南關，對抗延頭，遣一都督總諸軍節度，季冬進師，迄於春末，不過十旬，克之必矣。

translations.literal: then let the armies of the two Yu provinces seize Nan Pass directly, confront Yantou, send one commander-in-chief to coordinate all forces, advance in the last month of winter through the end of spring—in no more than a hundred days it will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: then let the two Yu armies seize Nan Pass and face Yantou, with one commander-in-chief directing all forces. March in the last month of winter through spring's end—within a hundred days it will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 」元英又奏稱：「今寶卷骨肉相殘，籓鎮鼎立。

translations.literal: " Yuan Ying memorialized again: "Now Baojuan's kin butcher one another, and the frontier commands stand like rival tripods.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Ying memorialized again: "Baojuan's own kin are at each other's throats, and the provincial strongholds stand like tripods in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 義陽孤絕，密邇王土，內無兵儲之固，外無糧援之期，此乃欲焚之鳥，不可去薪，授首之寇，豈容緩斧！

translations.literal: Yiyang is isolated and alone, pressed close to Our Dynasty's territory; within it has no solid stores of arms, without no prospect of grain relief—this is a bird that means to burn itself; one must not remove the kindling; a foe offering its head—how could one slow the axe!
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang stands alone, hard against our heartland. It has no secure stores of arms within, no hope of grain from without—a bird bent on burning itself: do not remove the kindling! A foe offering its head—why stay the axe?

sentences.zh: 若失此不取，豈惟後舉難圖，亦恐更為深患。

translations.literal: If we miss taking it now, not only will later efforts be hard to plan, I fear a still deeper calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If we let this chance slip, later campaigns will be harder—and I fear a worse calamity still.

sentences.zh: 今豫州刺史司馬悅已戒嚴垂發，東豫州刺史田益宗兵守三關，請遣軍司為之節度。

translations.literal: Now Inspector of Yu Sima Yue has declared martial alert and is about to march; Inspector of East Yu Tian Zongzong holds the Three Passes with troops—please send an army supervisor to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yu Sima Yue has already mobilized and is about to march; Inspector of East Yu Tian Zongzong holds the Three Passes. Please send an army supervisor to direct them.

sentences.zh: 」魏主乃遣直寢羊靈引為軍司。

translations.literal: " The Wei emperor then sent Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei emperor then sent Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 益宗遂入寇。

translations.literal: Zongzong then invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzong then invaded.

sentences.zh: 建寧太守黃天賜與益宗戰於赤亭，天賜敗績。

translations.literal: Jianning Administrator Huang Tianci fought Zongzong at Chiting; Tianci suffered a rout.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning Administrator Huang Tianci fought Zongzong at Chiting; Tianci was routed.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景之逼建康也，東昏候拜蔣子文為假黃鉞、使持節、相國、太宰、大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州牧、鐘山王；

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing pressed Jiankang, Marquis Donghun appointed Jiang Ziwen as Acting Yellow Battle-axe, Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yangzhou, and Prince of Mount Zhong;
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing pressed Jiankang, Marquis Donghun appointed Jiang Ziwen Acting Bearer of the Yellow Battle-axe, Envoy with the Staff of Full Powers, Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yangzhou, and Prince of Mount Zhong;

sentences.zh: 及衍至，又尊子文為靈帝，迎神像入後堂，使巫禱祀求福。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, he further honored Ziwen as Spirit Emperor, welcomed the idol into the rear hall, and had shamans pray and sacrifice for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan arrived, he further honored Ziwen as Spirit Emperor, brought the idol into the rear hall, and had shamans pray for blessing.

sentences.zh: 及城閉，城中軍事悉委王珍國；

translations.literal: When the city was shut, all military affairs within were entrusted to Wang Zhen'guo;
translations.idiomatic: When the city was closed, all military affairs in the capital were entrusted to Wang Zhen'guo;

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史張稷入衛京師，以稷為珍國之副。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Zhang Ji entered to guard the capital; Ji was made Zhen'guo's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yanzhou Zhang Ji came to defend the capital and was made Zhen'guo's deputy.

sentences.zh: 稷，瑰之弟也。

translations.literal: Ji was Gui's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the younger brother of Gui.

sentences.zh: 時城中實甲猶七萬人，東昏素好軍陳，與黃門、刀敕及宮人於華光殿前習戰鬥，詐作被創勢，使人以板□去，用為厭勝。

translations.literal: At the time there were still seventy thousand armored troops in the city. Donghun had always loved military formations; with Yellow Gate attendants, blade-guards, and palace women he practiced combat before Hua'guang Hall, feigning wounded posture, having people carry them away on boards [text damaged], using this for apotropaic rites.
translations.idiomatic: The city still had seventy thousand men under arms. Donghun had always loved war games; with Yellow Gate attendants, blade-guards, and palace women he drilled before Hua'guang Hall, feigning wounds and having them borne away on boards [lacuna in text] as a charm against evil.

sentences.zh: 常於殿中戎服、騎馬出入，以金銀為鎧冑，具裝飾以孔翠。

translations.literal: He often wore military garb in the hall, riding in and out, with gold and silver for armor, fully adorned with kingfisher feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He often wore military dress in the halls, riding in and out, with armor of gold and silver trimmed in kingfisher plumes.

sentences.zh: 晝眠夜起，一如平常。

translations.literal: Sleeping by day, rising by night, just as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He slept by day and rose by night, as if nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 聞外鼓叫聲，被大紅袍，登景陽樓屋上望之，弩幾中之。

translations.literal: Hearing drum and shout from outside, he threw on a great red robe, climbed to the roof of Jingyang Tower to look, and nearly was struck by a crossbow bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing drums and shouts outside, he threw on a great red robe, climbed to the roof of Jingyang Tower to watch, and nearly took a crossbow bolt.

sentences.zh: 始，東昏與左右謀，以為陳顯達一戰即敗，崔慧景圍城尋走，謂衍兵亦然，敕太官辦樵、米為百日調而已。

translations.literal: At first Donghun and his intimates plotted, believing that Chen Xianda had been routed in a single battle and Cui Huijing's siege of the city had soon fled, and that Yan's troops would likewise—he ordered the Imperial Kitchen to prepare firewood and rice for a hundred days' provisions, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: At first Donghun and his intimates assumed Chen Xianda had been beaten in one battle and Cui Huijing's siege would soon break—Yan's army would be no different. He ordered the Imperial Kitchen to stock firewood and rice for a hundred days, and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 及大桁之敗，眾情兇懼。

translations.literal: When the defeat at Daheng came, the mood of the masses turned savage with fear.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Daheng, panic seized the city.

sentences.zh: 茹法珍等恐士民逃潰，故閉城不復出兵。

translations.literal: Ru Fazhen and others feared soldiers and civilians would flee in collapse, so they shut the city and sent out no more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Fazhen and others, fearing soldiers and civilians would flee, shut the gates and sent out no more troops.

sentences.zh: 既而長圍已立，塹柵嚴固；

translations.literal: Before long the long encirclement was set, moats and palisades stern and firm;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the long siege was in place, moats and palisades tight;

sentences.zh: 然後出蕩，屢戰不捷。

translations.literal: only then did they sally to strike, repeatedly fighting without success.
translations.idiomatic: only then did they sally forth—and lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 東昏尤惜金錢，不肯賞賜；

translations.literal: Donghun was especially stingy with money and refused rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun was miserly with money and refused to reward anyone.

sentences.zh: 法珍叩頭請之，東昏曰：「賊來獨取我邪！

translations.literal: Fazhen kowtowed to beg for them; Donghun said, "When the rebels come do they take only me?
translations.idiomatic: Fazhen kowtowed to beg; Donghun said, "When the rebels come, do they want only me?

sentences.zh: 何為就我求物！

translations.literal: Why come to me asking for things!"
translations.idiomatic: Why come to me for things!"

sentences.zh: 」後堂儲數百具榜，啟為城防；

translations.literal: " Hundreds of planks were stored in the rear hall; [ministers] reported for use in city defense;
translations.idiomatic: " Hundreds of planks lay stored in the rear hall; officials proposed them for the city's defense;

sentences.zh: 東昏欲留作殿，竟不與。

translations.literal: Donghun wished to keep them for hall-building and in the end would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun wanted them for a new hall and would not release them.

sentences.zh: 又督御府作三百人精伏，待圍解以擬屏除，金銀雕鏤雜物，倍急於常。

translations.literal: He also supervised the Imperial Workshops to make three hundred elite hidden guards, awaiting the lifting of the siege for removing screens; gold, silver, carved and inlaid sundries—twice as urgent as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Imperial Workshops to fashion three hundred elite hidden guards for when the siege lifted, and gold and silver trinkets with twice the usual urgency.

sentences.zh: 眾皆怨怠，不為致力。

translations.literal: All were resentful and slack, unwilling to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone grumbled and slackened; no one would give his best.

sentences.zh: 外圍既久，城中皆思早亡，莫敢先發。

translations.literal: The outer siege having dragged on, everyone in the city longed for swift ruin, but none dared to act first.
translations.idiomatic: The siege wore on; all in the city wished for a quick end, but none dared strike first.

sentences.zh: 茹法珍、梅蟲兒說東昏曰：「大臣不留意，使圍不解，宜悉誅之。

translations.literal: Ru Fazhen and Mei Chong'er urged Donghun: "The great ministers pay no heed, so the siege will not be lifted—they should all be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Ru Fazhen and Mei Chong'er told Donghun, "The great ministers do nothing, so the siege never lifts—they should all be killed."

sentences.zh: 」王珍國、張稷懼禍，珍國密遣所親獻明鏡於蕭衍，衍斷金以報之。

translations.literal: " Wang Zhen'guo and Zhang Ji feared disaster; Zhen'guo secretly sent a close associate to present a bright mirror to Xiao Yan; Yan broke off a piece of gold to reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Zhen'guo and Zhang Ji feared for their lives. Zhen'guo secretly sent a confidant to offer Xiao Yan a bright mirror; Yan broke off gold in reply.

sentences.zh: 兗州中兵參軍馮翊張齊，稷之腹心也，珍國因齊密與稷謀同弒東昏。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Central Troops Commander Fufeng Zhang Qi was Ji's trusted confidant; Zhen'guo through Qi secretly plotted with Ji to jointly assassinate Donghun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi of Fufeng, Central Troops Commander of Yanzhou, was Ji's trusted man. Through Qi, Zhen'guo secretly plotted with Ji to kill Donghun together.

sentences.zh: 齊夜引珍國就稷，造膝定計，齊自執燭；

translations.literal: By night Qi led Zhen'guo to Ji; knee to knee they fixed the plan, Qi himself holding the candle.
translations.idiomatic: By night Qi brought Zhen'guo to Ji; knee to knee they fixed the plan, Qi holding the candle.

sentences.zh: 又以計告後閣舍人錢強。

translations.literal: He also told the plan to Rear Pavilion Attendant Qian Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also confided the plan to Rear Pavilion Attendant Qian Qiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙寅夜，強密令人開雲龍門，珍國、稷引兵入殿，御刀豐勇之為內應。

translations.literal: On the night of bingyin, the twelfth month, Qiang secretly had someone open Yunlong Gate; Zhen'guo and Ji led troops into the hall; Imperial Blade Feng Yongzhi was inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingyin in the twelfth month, Qiang secretly had Yunlong Gate opened. Zhen'guo and Ji led troops into the hall; Imperial Blade Feng Yongzhi was their man inside.

sentences.zh: 東昏在含德殿作笙歌，寢未熟，聞兵入，趨出北戶，欲還後宮，門已閉。

translations.literal: Donghun was at Hede Hall making reed-pipe music; his sleep was not yet deep; hearing troops enter, he rushed out the north door, wished to return to the inner palace—the gate was already shut.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun was at Hede Hall with music and song, not yet deep in sleep. Hearing troops enter, he ran out the north door toward the inner palace—but the gate was shut.

sentences.zh: 宦者黃泰平刀傷其膝，仆地，張齊斬之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Huang Taiping wounded his knee with a blade; he fell prostrate; Zhang Qi beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Huang Taiping cut his knee with a blade; he fell. Zhang Qi beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 稷召尚書右僕射王亮等列坐殿前西鐘下，令百僚署箋，以黃油裹東昏首，遣國子博士范雲等送詣石頭。

translations.literal: Ji summoned Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang and others to sit in ranks before the western bell in the hall-front, ordered the hundred officials to sign a petition, wrapped Donghun's head in yellow oilcloth, sent Imperial University Erudite Fan Yun and others to deliver it to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji summoned Wang Liang, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and others to sit before the western bell in the hall court, had the hundred officials sign a petition, wrapped Donghun's head in yellow oilcloth, and sent Imperial University Erudite Fan Yun and others to Shitou with it.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍王志歎曰：「冠雖弊，何可加足！

translations.literal: Right Guards General Wang Zhi sighed, "Though the cap is worn, how can you set foot upon it!"
translations.idiomatic: Right Guards General Wang Zhi sighed, "Though the cap is worn, how can one set foot upon it!"

sentences.zh: 」取庭中樹葉挼服之，偽悶，不署名。

translations.literal: " He took leaves from the courtyard tree, chewed and swallowed them, feigned fainting, and did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: " He took leaves from the courtyard tree, chewed and swallowed them, feigned collapse, and would not sign.

sentences.zh: 衍覽箋無志名，心嘉之。

translations.literal: Yan perused the petition, saw no Zhi's name, and inwardly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan read the petition, saw no name of Zhi, and inwardly approved.

sentences.zh: 亮，瑩之從弟；

translations.literal: Liang was Ying's younger cousin;
translations.idiomatic: Liang was the younger cousin of Ying;

sentences.zh: 志，僧虔之子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was Sengqian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was the son of Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 衍與范雲有舊，即留參帷幄。

translations.literal: Yan had old ties with Fan Yun and kept him to counsel at the planning tent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Fan Yun were old friends; he kept Yun to counsel him in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 王亮在東昏朝，以依違取容。

translations.literal: Wang Liang in Donghun's court had won favor through equivocation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang in Donghun's court had survived by equivocation.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍至新林，百僚皆間道送款，亮獨不遣。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan reached Xinlin, the hundred officials all sent pledges of allegiance by byways; Liang alone sent none.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan reached Xinlin, officials sent pledges of loyalty by secret paths; Liang alone sent none.

sentences.zh: 東昏敗，亮出見衍，衍曰：「顛而不扶，安用彼相！

translations.literal: Donghun defeated, Liang came out to see Yan; Yan said, "When one topples and you do not steady him, what use is such a minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Donghun fell; Liang came out to see Yan. Yan said, "When a man topples and you do not steady him, what use is such a minister!"

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「若其可扶，明公豈有今日之舉！

translations.literal: " Liang said, "If he could have been steadied, would Your Excellency have today's deed!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "If he could have been steadied, would Your Excellency have taken today's step!"

sentences.zh: 」城中出者，或被劫剝。

translations.literal: " Those who came out of the city were sometimes robbed and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who left the city were sometimes robbed and stripped.

sentences.zh: 楊公則親帥麾下陳於東掖門，衛送公卿士民，故出者多由公則營焉。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze personally led his followers and arrayed them at the East Yecha Gate, escorting and sending off ministers and commoners, so most who exited passed through Gongze's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze personally led his men and arrayed them at the East Yecha Gate, escorting ministers and commoners, so most who left went through Gongze's camp.

sentences.zh: 衍使張弘策先入清宮，封府庫及圖籍。

translations.literal: Yan sent Zhang Hongce ahead to enter and cleanse the palace, sealing the treasuries and archives.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Zhang Hongce ahead to enter the palace, seal the treasuries and archives.

sentences.zh: 於時城內珍寶委積，弘策禁勒部曲，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: At the time treasures within the city lay piled in heaps; Hongce restrained his troops—not the slightest hair was touched.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures lay heaped in the city; Hongce restrained his troops—not a hair was touched.

sentences.zh: 收潘妃及嬖臣茹法珍、梅蟲兒、王咺之等四十一人皆屬吏。

translations.literal: Pan Consort and favorite ministers Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Wang Xuanzhi, and forty-one others were all taken in charge by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Consort and favorites Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Wang Xuanzhi, and forty-one others were all handed to the law.

sentences.zh: 初，海陵王之廢也，王太后出居鄱陽王故第，號宣德宮。

translations.literal: At first when the Prince of Hailing was deposed, the queen dowager moved out to the former residence of the Prince of Poyang, called Xuande Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hailing was deposed, the queen dowager moved to the Prince of Poyang's former residence, called Xuande Palace.

sentences.zh: 己巳，蕭衍以宣德太后令追廢涪陵王為東昏侯，褚后及太子誦並為庶人。

translations.literal: On jisi, Xiao Yan by order of the Empress Dowager Xuande posthumously deposed the Prince of Fuling as Marquis Donghun; Empress Chu and Crown Prince Song were both made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, by order of Empress Dowager Xuande, Xiao Yan posthumously deposed the Prince of Fuling as Marquis Donghun; Empress Chu and Crown Prince Song were reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 以衍為中書監、大司馬、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，封建安郡公，依晉武陵王遵承製故事，百僚致敬；

translations.literal: Yan was made Secretariat Supervisor, Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Inspector of Yangzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Commandery Jian'an; following the precedent of Jin's Prince of Wuling Zun receiving and promulgating edicts—the hundred officials paid homage;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was made Secretariat Supervisor, Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Yangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Jian'an Commandery. Following Jin's precedent of Prince Wuling Zun receiving and issuing edicts, the hundred officials paid him homage;

sentences.zh: 以王亮為長史。

translations.literal: Wang Liang was made chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang was made chief steward.

sentences.zh: 壬申，更封建安王寶寅為鄱陽王。

translations.literal: On renshen, Prince Jian'an Bao Yin was recreated as Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Prince Jian'an Bao Yin was made Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以司徒、揚州刺史晉安王寶義為太尉，領司徒。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Grand Mentor and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi, was made Grand Commandant while retaining Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Grand Mentor and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi, was made Grand Commandant and continued as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 己卯，衍入屯閱武堂，下令大赦。

translations.literal: On jimao, Yan entered and encamped at Reviewing Arms Hall, ordered a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Yan entered and encamped at Reviewing Arms Hall and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 又下令：「凡昏制謬賦、淫刑濫役外，可詳檢前原，悉皆除蕩；

translations.literal: He also ordered: "Aside from Donghun's mistaken laws, absurd levies, licentious punishments, and abusive corvée, carefully investigate prior grounds and abolish them all entirely;
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered: "Aside from Donghun's mistaken statutes, absurd levies, cruel punishments, and abusive corvée, examine all prior grounds and abolish them;

sentences.zh: 其主守散失諸所損耗，精立科條，鹹從原例。

translations.literal: as for magistrates' losses and scattered wastage in various places, set detailed regulations and all follow the original statutes."
translations.idiomatic: for losses and waste under local magistrates, set clear rules and follow the original statutes."

sentences.zh: 」又下令：「通檢尚書眾曹，東昏時諸諍訟失理及主者淹停不時施行者，精加訊辨，依事議奏。

translations.literal: " He also ordered: "Thoroughly inspect all bureaus of the Masters of Writing; for contentious lawsuits from Donghun's time that were wrongly decided or delayed in execution by responsible officials, examine closely and report according to the facts."
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered: "Inspect all bureaus of the Masters of Writing; for lawsuits from Donghun's time wrongly decided or delayed by responsible officials, examine closely and report on each case."

sentences.zh: 」又下令：「收葬義師，掩瘞逆徒之死亡者。

translations.literal: " He also ordered: "Gather and bury the righteous troops; cover and inter the dead among the rebel host."
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered: "Bury the loyal dead and inter the fallen among the rebels."

sentences.zh: 潘妃有國色，衍欲留之，以問侍中、領軍將軍王茂，茂曰：「亡齊者此物，留之恐貽外議。

translations.literal: Pan Consort had national beauty; Yan wished to keep her, and asked Palace Attendant and Camp Commander Wang Mao; Mao said, "It was this creature that destroyed Qi; to keep her will likely invite outside criticism."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Consort was a national beauty; Yan wished to keep her and asked Palace Attendant and Camp Commander Wang Mao. Mao said, "This is what destroyed Qi; keeping her will invite outside talk."

sentences.zh: 」乃縊殺於獄，並誅嬖臣茹法珍等。

translations.literal: " She was then strangled in prison, and favorite ministers Ru Fazhen and others were likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: " She was strangled in prison, and favorites Ru Fazhen and others were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 以宮女二千賚將士。

translations.literal: Two thousand palace women were bestowed to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand palace women were bestowed to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以輔國將軍蕭宏為中護軍。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Assistant-General for the State Xiao Hong was made Central Camp Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Assistant-General for the State Xiao Hong was made Central Camp Commander.

sentences.zh: 衍之東下也，豫州刺史馬仙玭擁兵不附衍，衍使其故人姚仲賓說之，仙玭先為設酒，乃斬於軍門以徇。
